translations.idiomatic: Biography 13: Zhang Maodu

sentences.zh: 〈子永〉

translations.literal: 〈Son Yong〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Son Yong〉

translations.literal: Yu Dengzhi
translations.idiomatic: Yu Dengzhi

sentences.zh: 〈弟炳之〉

translations.literal: 〈Younger brother Bingzhi〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Younger brother Bingzhi〉

translations.literal: Xie Fangming; Jiang Yi
translations.idiomatic: Xie Fangming; Jiang Yi

sentences.zh: 張茂度

translations.literal: Zhang Maodu
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Maodu

sentences.zh: 張茂度，吳郡吳人，張良後也。

translations.literal: Zhang Maodu was a native of Wu in Wu commandery, a descendant of Zhang Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Maodu came from Wu in Wu commandery and was a descendant of Zhang Liang.

sentences.zh: 名與高祖諱同，故稱字。

translations.literal: His personal name was the same as Gaozu's taboo name, so he was called by his courtesy name.
translations.idiomatic: Because his personal name matched Gaozu's taboo, he was known by his courtesy name instead.

sentences.zh: 良七世孫為長沙太守，始遷于吳。

translations.literal: Liang's seventh-generation descendant served as Administrator of Changsha and first moved the family to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: A seventh-generation descendant of Liang served as Administrator of Changsha and was the first to relocate the line to Wu.

sentences.zh: 高祖嘉，曾祖澄，晉光祿大夫。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather was Jia; his great-great-grandfather Cheng was Jin Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather was Jia; his great-great-grandfather Cheng had been Grand Master of Splendid Happiness under Jin.

sentences.zh: 祖彭祖，廣州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Pengzu was Inspector of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Pengzu had served as Inspector of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 父敞，侍中、尚書、吳國內史。

translations.literal: His father Chang was Attendant-in-Ordinary, Minister, and Interior Governor of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chang had held the posts of Attendant-in-Ordinary, Minister, and Interior Governor of Wu.

sentences.zh: 茂度郡上計吏，主簿，功曹，州命從事史，竝不就。

translations.literal: Maodu was appointed commandery clerk for annual accounts, chief clerk, merit officer, and provincial staff aide, but accepted none of them.
translations.idiomatic: Maodu was offered the posts of commandery clerk for annual accounts, chief clerk, merit officer, and provincial staff aide, but he declined every one.

sentences.zh: 除琅邪王衛軍參軍，員外散騎侍郎，尚書度支郎，父憂不拜。

translations.literal: He was appointed Military Aide to the Guard General of the Prince of Langye, Extraordinary Cadet of the Scattered Cavalry, and Bureau Director of Revenue in the Ministry, but did not take office because of his father's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed military aide to the Prince of Langye's guard general, extraordinary cadet of the scattered cavalry, and a revenue post in the Ministry, but he did not take office while mourning his father.

sentences.zh: 服闋，為何無忌鎮南參軍。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he became Military Aide to Pacify the South under He Wuji.
translations.idiomatic: After his mourning period ended, he served as military aide on He Wuji's Pacify-the-South staff.

sentences.zh: 頃之，出補晉安太守，盧循為寇，覆沒江州，茂度及建安太守孫蚪之竝受其符書，供其調役。

translations.literal: Before long he was sent out to fill the post of Administrator of Jin'an. When Lu Xun raided and Jiangzhou fell, Maodu and the Administrator of Jian'an, Sun Douzhi, both received his sealed orders and supplied his levies and labor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was posted as Administrator of Jin'an. When Lu Xun's rebellion overran Jiangzhou, Maodu and Sun Douzhi, the Administrator of Jian'an, both received Lu's sealed orders and had to furnish his levies and corvée.

sentences.zh: 循走，俱坐免官。

translations.literal: When Xun fled, both were dismissed from office on that account.
translations.idiomatic: After Lu Xun withdrew, both men were dismissed from office on that account.

sentences.zh: 復以為始興相，郡經賊寇，廨宇焚燒，民物凋散，百不存一。

translations.literal: He was again made Chancellor of Shixing. The commandery had suffered bandit raids; government offices were burned, people and goods scattered, and scarcely one in a hundred remained.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed again as Chancellor of Shixing. The commandery had been ravaged by bandits: government buildings were burned, the population scattered, and scarcely one household in a hundred remained.

sentences.zh: 茂度創立城寺，弔死撫傷，收集離散，民戶漸復。

translations.literal: Maodu founded city walls and temples, mourned the dead and comforted the wounded, gathered the scattered, and households gradually returned.
translations.idiomatic: Maodu rebuilt walls and temples, mourned the dead and cared for the wounded, gathered the scattered population, and households gradually returned.

sentences.zh: 在郡一周，徵為太尉參軍，尋轉主簿、揚州治中從事史。

translations.literal: After one full year in the commandery he was summoned as Military Aide to the Grand Commandant, and soon transferred to chief clerk and Senior Clerk for Administration of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After a full year in office he was summoned as military aide to the Grand Commandant, and soon became chief clerk and senior administrative aide for Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 高祖西伐劉毅，茂度居守。

translations.literal: When Gaozu marched west against Liu Yi, Maodu remained to guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu marched west against Liu Yi, Maodu stayed behind to hold the capital.

sentences.zh: 留州事悉委之。

translations.literal: All provincial affairs left behind were entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: He was entrusted with all provincial affairs during the campaign.

sentences.zh: 軍還，遷中書侍郎。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was promoted to Gentleman of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, he was promoted to gentleman of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 出為司馬休之平西司馬、河南太守。

translations.literal: He went out as Pacify-the-West Major under Sima Xiuzhi and as Administrator of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as major on Sima Xiuzhi's Pacify-the-West staff and as Administrator of Henan.

sentences.zh: 高祖將討休之，茂度聞知，乘輕船逃下，逢高祖於中路，以為錄事參軍，太守如故。

translations.literal: When Gaozu was about to attack Xiuzhi, Maodu heard of it, took a light boat and fled downstream, met Gaozu on the way, and was made Recording Army Aide; his post as Administrator remained unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Gaozu was about to attack Xiuzhi, Maodu fled downstream in a light boat, met Gaozu on the march, and was appointed recording army aide while retaining his post as Administrator.

sentences.zh: 江陵平，驃騎將軍道憐為荊州，茂度仍為諮議參軍，太守如故。

translations.literal: When Jiangling was pacified, Flying Cavalry General Daolian took Jingzhou; Maodu remained Consultation Army Aide, and his post as Administrator was unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiangling was pacified, Flying Cavalry General Daolian was assigned to Jingzhou; Maodu continued as consultation army aide and kept his post as Administrator.

sentences.zh: 還為揚州別駕從事史。

translations.literal: He returned to serve as Senior Clerk Attached to the Chief Administrator of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to Yangzhou as senior clerk attached to the chief administrator.

sentences.zh: 高祖北伐關洛，復任留州事。

translations.literal: When Gaozu marched north against Guan and Luo, he again entrusted him with provincial affairs left behind.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu marched north against Guan and Luo, Maodu was again left in charge of provincial affairs.

sentences.zh: 出為使持節、督廣、交二州諸軍事、建武將軍、平越中郎將、廣州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out bearing the staff of authority, as Supervisor of military affairs in Guang and Jiao provinces, Establishing Martial General, Pacify-the-Yue Central Bulwark General, and Inspector of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted with the staff of authority as supervisor of military affairs in Guang and Jiao, as Establishing Martial General and Pacify-the-Yue central bulwark general, and as Inspector of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 綏靜百越，嶺外安之。

translations.literal: He pacified the Hundred Yue, and beyond the ranges there was peace.
translations.idiomatic: He pacified the Yue peoples, and the lands beyond the mountain ranges were settled.

sentences.zh: 以疾求還，復為道憐司馬。

translations.literal: On grounds of illness he asked to return and again became Daolian's major.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to return on grounds of illness and again served as major on Daolian's staff.

sentences.zh: 丁繼母憂，服闋，除廷尉，轉尚書吏部郎。

translations.literal: He entered mourning for his stepmother; when mourning ended he was appointed Commandant of Justice and transferred to Bureau Director of Personnel in the Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his stepmother he was appointed Commandant of Justice, then transferred to director of the Ministry's personnel bureau.

sentences.zh: 茂度內足於財，自絕人事，經始本縣之華山以為居止，優遊野澤，如此者七年。

translations.literal: Maodu was inwardly sufficient in wealth, cut himself off from worldly affairs, founded a dwelling on Mount Hua in his home county, and roamed fields and marshes at leisure for seven years.
translations.idiomatic: Maodu had ample private means, withdrew from public life, built a home on Mount Hua in his home county, and for seven years wandered the countryside at leisure.

sentences.zh: 十八年，除會稽太守。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was appointed Administrator of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year of the reign he was appointed Administrator of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 素有吏能，在郡縣，職事甚理。

translations.literal: He had long had administrative ability; in commanderies and counties his duties were very well ordered.
translations.idiomatic: He had long been known for administrative skill, and in every commandery or county his office ran in good order.

sentences.zh: 明年，卒官，時年六十七。

translations.literal: The next year he died in office, aged sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he died in office, at the age of sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 諡曰恭子。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Gongzi.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title Gongzi.

sentences.zh: 茂度同郡陸仲元者，晉太尉玩曾孫也。

translations.literal: Lu Zhongyuan of the same commandery as Maodu was a great-grandson of Jin Grand Commandant Wan.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhongyuan, a man of the same commandery as Maodu, was a great-grandson of Jin Grand Commandant Wan.

sentences.zh: 以事用見知，歷清資，吏部郎，右衛將軍，侍中，吳郡太守。

translations.literal: Through practical ability he won notice, passed through pure posts, became Bureau Director of Personnel, Right Guard General, Attendant-in-Ordinary, and Administrator of Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His practical ability won recognition; he rose through prestigious posts to director of personnel, Right Guard General, Attendant-in-Ordinary, and Administrator of Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 自玩洎仲元，四世為侍中，時人方之金、張二族。

translations.literal: From Wan down to Zhongyuan, four generations served as Attendant-in-Ordinary; people of the time compared them to the Jin and Zhang clans.
translations.idiomatic: From Wan to Zhongyuan, four generations held the post of Attendant-in-Ordinary, and contemporaries ranked the family with the Jin and Zhang clans.

sentences.zh: 弟子真，元嘉十年，為海陵太守。

translations.literal: His younger clansman Zhen, in the tenth year of Yuanjia, was Administrator of Hailing.
translations.idiomatic: His younger kinsman Zhen became Administrator of Hailing in the tenth year of Yuanjia.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人狄當為太祖所信委，家在海陵，死還葬，橋路毀壞，不通喪車，縣求發民脩治，子真不許。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Di Dang was trusted by Taizu; his family was in Hailing. When he died and was brought back for burial, bridges and roads were ruined and funeral carts could not pass. The county asked to mobilize the people to repair them; Zizhen did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Di Dang, whom Taizu trusted, was from Hailing. When he died and his body was brought home for burial, ruined bridges and roads blocked the funeral procession. The county wanted to draft laborers for repairs, but Zizhen refused.

sentences.zh: 司徒彭城王義康聞而善之，召為國子博士，司徒左西掾，州治中，臨海東陽太守。

translations.literal: Prince of Pengcheng Yikang, Minister of Education, heard and approved, and summoned him as Erudite of the Imperial University, Left Western Aide of the Minister of Education, Senior Clerk for Administration of the province, and Administrator of Linhai and Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Pengcheng Yikang, the Minister of Education, approved and summoned him as erudite of the Imperial University, left western aide on the minister's staff, senior provincial administrative aide, and Administrator of Linhai and Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 茂度子演，太子中舍人；

translations.literal: Maodu's son Yan was Palace Attendant of the Heir Apparent;
translations.idiomatic: Maodu's son Yan served as palace attendant to the heir apparent;

sentences.zh: 演弟鏡，新安太守，皆有盛名，並早卒。

translations.literal: Yan's younger brother Jing was Administrator of Xin'an; both had great fame and both died young.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's younger brother Jing was Administrator of Xin'an; both were highly regarded and both died young.

sentences.zh: 鏡弟永。

translations.literal: Jing's younger brother Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Jing's younger brother was Yong.

sentences.zh: 永字景雲，初為郡主簿，州從事，轉司徒士曹參軍，出補餘姚令，入為尚書中兵郎。

translations.literal: Yong, courtesy name Jingyun, first served as commandery chief clerk and provincial staff member, then transferred to Military Aide in the Minister of Education's office, went out to fill the post of Magistrate of Yuyao, and entered as Central Military Bureau Director in the Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Yong, courtesy name Jingyun, began as commandery chief clerk and provincial staff member, then became military aide in the Minister of Education's office, was posted as magistrate of Yuyao, and entered the central military bureau of the Ministry.

sentences.zh: 先是，尚書中條制繁雜，元嘉十八年，欲加治撰，徙永為刪定郎，掌其任。

translations.literal: Earlier, regulations in the central Ministry were numerous and tangled. In the eighteenth year of Yuanjia they wished to revise and compile them; Yong was moved to Editing and Revision Officer and charged with the task.
translations.idiomatic: The central Ministry's regulations had grown tangled; in the eighteenth year of Yuanjia the court planned a thorough revision, and Yong was made editing officer to oversee it.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，除建康令，所居皆有稱績。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was appointed Magistrate of Jiankang; in every post he won praise for achievement.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he was appointed magistrate of Jiankang, and in every post he earned a reputation for solid performance.

sentences.zh: 又除廣陵王誕北中郎錄事參軍。

translations.literal: He was again appointed Recording Army Aide to the North Central Bulwark of Prince of Guangling Dan.
translations.idiomatic: He was also appointed recording army aide on Prince of Guangling Dan's North Central Bulwark staff.

sentences.zh: 永涉獵書史，能為文章，善隸書，曉音律，騎射雜藝，觸類兼善，又有巧思，益為太祖所知。

translations.literal: Yong ranged through books and histories, could write essays, was skilled at clerical script, understood music, and in riding, archery, and miscellaneous arts excelled in every kind; he also had ingenious ideas and came to be still more known to Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Yong read widely in history, wrote well, excelled at clerical script, understood music, and was accomplished in horsemanship, archery, and other arts besides; his ingenuity won him still greater favor with Taizu.

sentences.zh: 紙及墨皆自營造，上每得永表啟，輒執玩咨嗟，自歎供御者了不及也。

translations.literal: He made paper and ink himself. Whenever the emperor received Yong's memorials, he would take them, admire them, and sigh that the palace suppliers fell utterly short.
translations.idiomatic: He made his own paper and ink. Whenever the emperor received Yong's memorials he would admire them and lament that the palace workshops could not match them.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，造華林園、玄武湖，並使永監統。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year the Hualin Garden and Xuanwu Lake were built, and Yong was put in charge of both.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year the Hualin Garden and Xuanwu Lake were constructed, with Yong supervising both projects.

sentences.zh: 凡諸制置，皆受則於永。

translations.literal: In all arrangements and installations, standards were taken from Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Every design and installation followed standards set by Yong.

sentences.zh: 徙為江夏王義恭太尉中兵參軍、越騎校尉、振武將軍、廣陵、南沛二郡太守。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Central Military Aide on Prince of Jiangxia Yigong's Grand Commandant staff, Colonel of the Yue Cavalry, Quelling Martial General, and Administrator of Guangling and Nanpei.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to central military aide on Prince of Jiangxia Yigong's Grand Commandant staff, made Colonel of the Yue Cavalry and Quelling Martial General, and appointed Administrator of Guangling and Nanpei.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，又除江夏王義恭驃騎中兵參軍，沛郡如故。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was again appointed Central Military Aide on Prince of Jiangxia Yigong's Flying Cavalry staff; his post in Pei commandery was unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year he was again appointed central military aide on Yigong's Flying Cavalry staff while retaining his post in Pei commandery.

sentences.zh: 永既有才能，所在每盡心力，太祖謂堪為將。

translations.literal: Yong had both talent and ability; in every post he gave his full mind and strength, and Taizu said he was fit to be a general.
translations.idiomatic: Yong had talent and drive; in every post he gave his all, and Taizu judged him fit for command.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，以永督冀州、青州之濟南、樂安、太原三郡諸軍事、揚威將軍、冀州刺史，督王玄謨、申坦等諸將，經略河南。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year Yong was made Supervisor of military affairs in Ji and the three commanderies of Jinan, Le'an, and Taiyuan in Qing province, Raising Might General, and Inspector of Ji, directing generals Wang Xuanmo, Shen Tan, and others to plan operations south of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year Yong was put in charge of Ji province and the Jinan, Le'an, and Taiyuan districts of Qing, with the title Raising Might General and Inspector of Ji, and directed Wang Xuanmo, Shen Tan, and other generals in operations south of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 攻碻磝城，累旬不能拔。

translations.literal: They attacked the city of Que'ao; for many tens of days they could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: They besieged Que'ao for many weeks without taking it.

sentences.zh: 其年八月七日夜，虜開門燒樓及攻車，士卒燒死及為虜所殺甚眾，永即夜撤圍退軍，不報告諸將，眾軍驚擾，為虜所乘，死敗塗地；

translations.literal: On the night of the seventh day of the eighth month that year the barbarians opened the gates, burned the towers and assault wagons, and very many soldiers were burned to death or killed by the barbarians. Yong that same night lifted the siege and withdrew, without informing the other generals. The armies were thrown into alarm and disorder, the barbarians pressed the advantage, and death and defeat spread everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of the seventh day of the eighth month the enemy sallied, burning the siege towers and assault engines; many men were burned or killed. Yong withdrew that same night without informing the other commanders. The armies panicked, the enemy pressed the rout, and the slaughter was catastrophic.

sentences.zh: 永及申坦並為統府撫軍將軍蕭思話所收，繫於歷城獄。

translations.literal: Yong and Shen Tan were both taken into custody by Pacifying Army General Xiao Sihua of the supreme command and imprisoned in Licheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yong and Shen Tan were both arrested by Pacifying Army General Xiao Sihua, commander of the campaign, and imprisoned at Licheng.

sentences.zh: 太祖以屢征無功，諸將不可任，責永等與思話詔曰：「虜既乘利，方向盛冬，若脫敢送死，兄弟父子，自共當之耳。

translations.literal: Because repeated campaigns had no success and the generals could not be entrusted, Taizu blamed Yong and the others and issued an edict to Sihua saying: "The barbarians have seized the advantage and are heading into deep winter. If they should dare to risk death, brothers and fathers and sons will answer for it together."
translations.idiomatic: Taizu, furious that repeated campaigns had failed and that his generals could not be trusted, sent Sihua an edict blaming Yong and the others: "The enemy has the advantage and winter is coming. If they dare to fight to the death, let brothers and fathers and sons answer for it together."

sentences.zh: 言及增憤，可以示張永、申坦。

translations.literal: Speaking of it only increased his rage; it may be shown to Zhang Yong and Shen Tan.
translations.idiomatic: Even to speak of it only deepened his anger; let Zhang Yong and Shen Tan see this edict."

sentences.zh: 」又與江夏王義恭書曰：「早知諸將輩如此，恨不以白刃驅之，今者悔何所及！」

translations.literal: He also wrote to Prince of Jiangxia Yigong: "Had I known earlier that these generals would be like this, I would regret not driving them with naked blades. What is there left to regret now!"
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote to Prince of Jiangxia Yigong: "Had I known these generals would perform so poorly, I would have driven them forward at sword point. Now what regret can avail?"

sentences.zh: 三十年，元兇弑立，起永督青州、徐州之東安、東莞二郡諸軍事、輔國將軍、青州刺史。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year the regicide Yuanxiong seized the throne; Yong was raised to supervise military affairs in Qing and the two commanderies of Dong'an and Dongguan in Xu, made Assisting the State General, and appointed Inspector of Qing.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year, after the regicide Yuanxiong seized the throne, Yong was recalled to supervise Qing and the Dong'an and Dongguan districts of Xu as Assisting the State General and Inspector of Qing.

sentences.zh: 司空南譙王義宣起義，又板永為督冀州、青州之濟南、樂安、太原三郡諸軍事、輔國將軍、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Prince of Nanqiao Yixuan rose in righteous arms, and again appointed Yong by board to supervise military affairs in Ji and the three commanderies of Jinan, Le'an, and Taiyuan in Qing, as Assisting the State General and Inspector of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: When Minister of Works Prince of Nanqiao Yixuan raised the banner of revolt, he again commissioned Yong to command Ji and the Jinan, Le'an, and Taiyuan districts as Assisting the State General and Inspector of Ji.

sentences.zh: 永遣司馬崔勳之、中兵參軍劉則二軍馳赴國難。

translations.literal: Yong sent his major Cui Xunzhi and Central Military Aide Liu Ze with two armies to hurry to the state's peril.
translations.idiomatic: Yong sent his major Cui Xunzhi and central military aide Liu Ze with two armies to rush to the capital's defense.

sentences.zh: 時蕭思話在彭城，義宣慮二人不相諧緝，與思話書，勸與永坦懷。

translations.literal: At the time Xiao Sihua was at Pengcheng; Yixuan feared the two would not work in harmony and wrote to Sihua urging open-hearted reconciliation with Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Sihua was then at Pengcheng; fearing the two men would not cooperate, Yixuan wrote urging Sihua to reconcile openly with Yong.

sentences.zh: 又使永從兄長史張暢與永書曰：「近有都信，具汝刑網之原，可謂雖在縲絏，而腹心無愧矣。

translations.literal: He also had Yong's elder cousin's son Chief Clerk Zhang Chang write to Yong: "A recent capital dispatch fully set forth the reasons for your legal troubles. One may say that though you were in bonds, your heart had no shame."
translations.idiomatic: He also had Zhang Chang, chief clerk and Yong's elder cousin, write to him: "A recent dispatch from the capital explained the reasons for your imprisonment. Though you were in chains, your conscience was clear."

sentences.zh: 蕭公平厚，先無嫌隙，見汝翰跡，言不相傷，何其滔滔稱人意邪！

translations.literal: Xiao is fair and generous; there was no prior grudge. Seeing your handwriting, he said he would not harm you—how abundantly it pleased people!
translations.idiomatic: Xiao is fair-minded and there was no old grudge between you. He saw your letter and said he bore you no ill will—how warmly he spoke in your favor!

sentences.zh: 當今世故艱迫，義旗雲起，方藉群賢，共康時難。

translations.literal: Now the times are hard and pressing; righteous banners rise like clouds. We rely on worthy men together to bring peace to the age's troubles.
translations.idiomatic: These are perilous times and righteous armies are rising everywhere; we need worthy men together to restore order.

sentences.zh: 當遠慕廉、藺在公之德，近效平、勃忘私之美，忽此蒂芥，克申舊情。

translations.literal: You should look far to Lian Po and Lin Xiangru's public-minded virtue and take near example from Chen Ping and Zhou Bo's beauty of forgetting private wrongs; set aside this thorn of resentment and renew your old friendship.
translations.idiomatic: Take as your distant models Lian Po and Lin Xiangru, who set the public good above private grievance, and as your near models Chen Ping and Zhou Bo, who forgot personal slights; put aside this petty resentment and renew your old bond.

sentences.zh: 公亦命蕭示以疏達，兼令相報，共遵此旨。

translations.literal: The prince also ordered Xiao to show openness and generosity, and further to exchange replies, all following this intent."
translations.idiomatic: The prince has also told Xiao to be open with you and to exchange letters so that you may both follow this course."

sentences.zh: 」事平，召為江夏王義恭大司馬從事中郎，領中兵。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled he was summoned as Attendant Gentleman on Prince of Jiangxia Yigong's Grand Marshal staff, concurrently heading the central military office.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion was suppressed he was summoned as attendant gentleman on Prince of Jiangxia Yigong's Grand Marshal staff, with charge of the central military office.

sentences.zh: 時使百僚獻讜言，永以為宜立諫官，開不諱之路，講師旅，示安不忘危。

translations.literal: At the time all officials were ordered to submit candid counsel. Yong held that remonstrating officers should be established, the road of no taboo opened, armies drilled, and in peace danger not forgotten.
translations.idiomatic: When the court called for candid advice from all officials, Yong argued for remonstrating officers, frank speech without fear, regular military drill, and the principle that in peace one must not forget peril.

sentences.zh: 世祖孝建元年，臧質反，遣永輔武昌王渾鎮京口。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xiaojian under Shizu, Zang Zhi rebelled; Yong was sent to assist Prince of Wuchang Hun in guarding Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xiaojian, when Zang Zhi rebelled, Yong was sent to assist Prince of Wuchang Hun in holding Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 其年，出為揚州別駕從事史。

translations.literal: That same year he went out as Senior Clerk Attached to the Chief Administrator of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he was posted as senior clerk attached to the chief administrator of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，召入為尚書左丞。

translations.literal: The next year he was summoned in as Left Assistant Minister in the Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was summoned to the Ministry as left assistant minister.

sentences.zh: 時將士休假，年開三番，紛紜道路。

translations.literal: At the time officers and soldiers took leave three times a year, crowding the roads in confusion.
translations.idiomatic: Officers and soldiers were then granted leave three times a year, and the roads were thronged with travelers.

sentences.zh: 永建議曰：「臣聞開兵從稼，前王以之兼隙，耕戰遞勞，先代以之經遠。

translations.literal: Yong submitted a proposal: "Your servant has heard that opening armies from farming, former kings used to fill the intervals; farming and fighting alternated in labor, and former ages thereby planned for the long term."
translations.idiomatic: Yong submitted a memorial: "I have read that ancient kings drew soldiers from the fields in the intervals between campaigns, alternating farm work with military service so that the state could plan for the long term."

sentences.zh: 當今化寧萬里，文同九服，捐金走驥，於焉自始。

translations.literal: Now transformation is tranquil for ten thousand li, writing is uniform in the nine domains, and abandoning arms and running horses begins from here.
translations.idiomatic: Today the realm is at peace for ten thousand li and culture is uniform across the nine domains; it is time to lay aside arms and let horses run free in the fields."

sentences.zh: 伏見將士休假，多蒙三番，程會既促，裝赴在早。

translations.literal: Your servant observes that soldiers on leave often receive three rounds; schedules are already tight and outfitting and departure come early.
translations.idiomatic: Yet soldiers are often granted three leaves a year; schedules are tight and they must pack and depart early."

sentences.zh: 故一歲之間，四馳遙路，或失遽春耜，或違要秋登，致使公替常儲，家闕舊粟，考定利害，宜加詳改。

translations.literal: Thus within one year they race four times along distant roads, sometimes missing urgent spring plowing or crucial autumn harvest, so that public granaries lack regular stores and households lack old grain. Weighing benefit and harm, detailed reform should be added.
translations.idiomatic: Within a single year they may travel the roads four times, missing spring plowing or the autumn harvest, so public granaries run short and households lose their stored grain. Weighing the costs, the policy should be revised in detail."

sentences.zh: 愚謂交代之限，以一年為制，使征士之念，勞未及積；

translations.literal: Your servant proposes that the term of rotation be fixed at one year, so that campaigning soldiers' thoughts of toil have not yet piled up;
translations.idiomatic: I propose that the rotation period be fixed at one year, so that soldiers on campaign are not worn down by accumulated fatigue;

sentences.zh: 游農之望，收功歲成。

translations.literal: and roving farmers' hopes may gather harvest within the year.
translations.idiomatic: and farmers who also serve may complete their harvest within the year."

sentences.zh: 斯則王度無騫，民業斯植矣。

translations.literal: Then the royal measure will not falter and the people's livelihood will be established.
translations.idiomatic: Then the royal standard will stand firm and the people's livelihood will take root."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: The proposal was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The court accepted his proposal.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，除吏部尚書。

translations.literal: When Taizong took the throne, Yong was appointed Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong took the throne, Yong was appointed Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 未拜，會四方反叛，復以為吳興太守，加冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: Before he took office, rebellion broke out on all sides; he was again made Administrator of Wuxing and promoted to Champion General.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take office, rebellions erupted across the realm; he was again appointed Administrator of Wuxing with the rank of Champion General.

sentences.zh: 假節。

translations.literal: He was given provisional credentials.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted provisional credentials.

sentences.zh: 未拜，以將軍假節，徙為吳郡太守，率軍東討。

translations.literal: Before taking office, bearing the general's provisional credentials, he was transferred to Administrator of Wu commandery and led an army east to suppress.
translations.idiomatic: Again before taking office, he was transferred to Administrator of Wu commandery with provisional credentials and led troops east to suppress the rebels.

sentences.zh: 又為散騎常侍、太子詹事。

translations.literal: He was again made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Steward of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was also appointed regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and steward of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 未拜，遷使持節、監青、冀、幽、并四州諸軍事、前將軍，青、冀二州刺史，統諸將討徐州刺史薛安都，累戰克捷，破薛索兒等，事在安都傳。

translations.literal: Before taking office he was transferred to bearer of the staff of authority, Overseer of military affairs in Qing, Ji, You, and Bing provinces, Forward General, and Inspector of Qing and Ji, directing the generals against Xuzhou Inspector Xue Andu; in repeated battles he won victories and defeated Xue Suo'er and others—the matter is in Andu's biography.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take those posts he was transferred with the staff of authority to oversee Qing, Ji, You, and Bing, as Forward General and Inspector of Qing and Ji, commanding the campaign against Xuzhou Inspector Xue Andu; he won repeated victories over Xue Suo'er and others, as recounted in Andu's biography.

sentences.zh: 又遷散騎常侍、鎮軍將軍、太子詹事，權領徐州刺史。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Pacifying Army General, Steward of the Heir Apparent, and acting Inspector of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, Pacifying Army General, and steward of the heir apparent, with acting authority as Inspector of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 又都督徐、兗、青、冀四州諸軍事，又為使持節、都督南兗、徐二州諸軍事、南兗州刺史，常侍、將軍如故。

translations.literal: He was again made Commander of military affairs in Xu, Yan, Qing, and Ji, and again bearer of the staff of authority as Commander of military affairs in Southern Yan and Xu and Inspector of Southern Yan; his posts as regular attendant and general were unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was made commander of military affairs in Xu, Yan, Qing, and Ji, then bearer of the staff as commander of Southern Yan and Xu and Inspector of Southern Yan, retaining his posts as regular attendant and general.

sentences.zh: 時薛安都據彭城請降，而誠心不款，太宗遣永與沈攸之以重兵迎之，加督前鋒軍事，進軍彭城。

translations.literal: At the time Xue Andu held Pengcheng and asked to surrender, but his sincerity was not open; Taizong sent Yong and Shen Youzhi with a heavy force to receive him, added supervision of vanguard military affairs, and advanced on Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Andu then held Pengcheng and offered to surrender, but his sincerity was doubtful; Taizong sent Yong and Shen Youzhi with a large force to receive him, put Yong in charge of the vanguard, and marched on Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 安都招引索虜之兵既至，士卒離散，永狼狽引軍還，為虜所追，大敗。

translations.literal: When Andu had drawn the northern barbarians and their troops arrived, the soldiers scattered; Yong withdrew his army in disarray, was pursued by the barbarians, and suffered a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: When Andu brought in the northern tribes and their troops arrived, Yong's army disintegrated; he withdrew in disorder, was pursued, and suffered a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 復值寒雪，士卒離散，永腳指斷落，僅以身免，失其第四子。

translations.literal: They again met with cold snow; soldiers scattered; Yong's toes froze off; he barely escaped with his life and lost his fourth son.
translations.idiomatic: A blizzard added to the rout; Yong lost toes to frostbite, barely escaped with his life, and lost his fourth son.

sentences.zh: 三年，徙都督會稽、東陽、臨海、永嘉、新安五郡諸軍事、會稽太守，將軍如故。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to Commander of military affairs in the five commanderies of Kuaiji, Dongyang, Linhai, Yongjia, and Xin'an, and Administrator of Kuaiji; his rank as general was unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was transferred to command the five commanderies of Kuaiji, Dongyang, Linhai, Yongjia, and Xin'an as Administrator of Kuaiji, retaining his general's rank.

sentences.zh: 以北討失律，固求自貶，降號左將軍。

translations.literal: Because of failure in discipline on the northern campaign, he firmly asked to demote himself and was reduced to Left General.
translations.idiomatic: After his defeat in the northern campaign he insisted on demotion and was reduced to Left General.

sentences.zh: 永痛悼所失之子，有兼常哀，服制雖除，猶立靈座，飲食衣服，待之如生。

translations.literal: Yong grieved deeply for the son he had lost, with grief beyond the ordinary; though mourning garments were removed, he still maintained a spirit seat, and in food, drink, and clothing treated him as if alive.
translations.idiomatic: Yong mourned his dead son with grief that went beyond ordinary sorrow. Even after the mourning period ended, he kept a spirit seat and continued to set out food, drink, and clothing for the boy as though he were still alive.

sentences.zh: 每出行，常別具名車好馬，號曰侍從，有事輒語左右報郎君。

translations.literal: Whenever he went out, he would specially prepare a fine carriage and good horses, calling them his attendants; when something occurred he would tell those beside him to report to the young master.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he went out, he had a separate fine carriage and horses set aside, which he called his son's attendants; if anything happened, he would tell his servants to report it to the young master.

sentences.zh: 以破薛索兒功，封孝昌縣侯，食邑千戶。

translations.literal: For merit in defeating Xue Suo'er, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiaochang with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: For defeating Xue Suo'er he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiaochang with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 在會稽，賓客有謝方童等，坐贓下獄死，永又降號冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: While in Kuaiji, guests of his including Xie Fangtong were imprisoned and died on charges of corruption, and Yong was again demoted to Champion General.
translations.idiomatic: While serving in Kuaiji, his guests Xie Fangtong and others were imprisoned and executed for corruption, and Yong was demoted again to Champion General.

sentences.zh: 四年，遷使持節、督雍、梁、南北秦四州、郢州之竟陵、隨二郡諸軍事、右將軍、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was transferred to Bearer of the Staff, Commander of military affairs in Yong, Liang, North and South Qin four provinces and the commanderies of Jingling and Sui in Yingzhou, Right General, and Inspector of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was appointed Bearer of the Staff, commander of military affairs in Yong, Liang, North and South Qin, and the Jingling and Sui commanderies of Yingzhou, as Right General and Inspector of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 未拜，停為太子詹事，加散騎常侍、本州大中正。

translations.literal: Before assuming the post he was retained as Grand Master of the Crown Prince's Household, with additional appointments as Regular Attendant of the Scatterers and Chief Rectifier of his native province.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up the post he was kept at court as Grand Master of the Crown Prince's Household, with additional appointments as Regular Attendant of the Scatterers and Chief Rectifier of his native province.

sentences.zh: 六年，又加護軍將軍，領石頭戍事；

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was further made Guardian General and put in charge of the garrison at Stone City;
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was further made Guardian General and put in charge of the Stone City garrison;

sentences.zh: 給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: and granted one set of drum-and-pipe music.
translations.idiomatic: and granted a set of drum-and-pipe musicians.

sentences.zh: 七年，遷金紫光祿大夫，尋復領護軍。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to Grand Master of Glorious Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon; soon afterward he again headed the Guardians.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was promoted to Grand Master of Glorious Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and soon afterward resumed command of the Guardians.

sentences.zh: 後廢帝即位，進右光祿大夫，加侍中，領安成王師，加親信二十人。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor succeeded to the throne, Yong was promoted to Right Grand Master of Glorious Happiness, made Palace Attendant, appointed Preceptor to the Prince of Ancheng, and granted twenty personal attendants.
translations.idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne, Yong was promoted to Right Grand Master of Glorious Happiness, made Palace Attendant and Preceptor to the Prince of Ancheng, and granted twenty personal attendants.

sentences.zh: 又領本州中正，出為吳郡太守，秩中二千石，侍中、右光祿如故。

translations.literal: He also headed the Rectifier of his native province and went out as Administrator of Wu Commandery, with salary at the middle two-thousand-dan grade; his posts as Palace Attendant and Right Grand Master of Glorious Happiness were unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as Chief Rectifier of his native province and was sent out as Administrator of Wu Commandery at the middle two-thousand-dan salary grade, retaining his posts as Palace Attendant and Right Grand Master of Glorious Happiness.

sentences.zh: 元徽二年，遷使持節、都督南兗、徐、青、冀、益五州諸軍事、征北將軍、南兗州刺史，侍中如故。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanhui he was transferred to Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of military affairs in the five provinces of South Yan, Xu, Qing, Ji, and Yi, General Who Conquers the North, and Inspector of South Yanzhou; his post as Palace Attendant was unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuanhui he was appointed Bearer of the Staff and commander-in-chief of military affairs in South Yan, Xu, Qing, Ji, and Yi, as General Who Conquers the North and Inspector of South Yanzhou, retaining his post as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 永少便驅馳，志在宣力，年雖已老，志氣未衰，優遊閑任，意甚不樂，及有此授，喜悅非常，即日命駕還都。

translations.literal: Yong had been skilled at riding from youth and was eager to exert himself in service; though old in years, his spirit had not faded. In easy, idle posts he was very discontented; when he received this appointment he was overjoyed and that same day ordered his carriage and returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yong had been a skilled rider since youth and was eager to serve in the field. Though advanced in years, his fighting spirit had not waned, and he had been deeply unhappy in easy, idle posts. When this appointment came he was overjoyed and that same day ordered his carriage back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 未之鎮，值桂陽王休範作亂，永率所領出屯白下。

translations.literal: Before he took up his post at the province, the Prince of Guiyang, Xiu Fan, rose in rebellion; Yong led the troops under his command out to encamp at Baixia.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up his provincial post, the Prince of Guiyang, Xiu Fan, rebelled, and Yong led his troops out to encamp at Baixia.

sentences.zh: 休範至新亭，大桁不守，前鋒遂攻南掖門。

translations.literal: When Xiu Fan reached Xinting, the Great Bridge was not held, and the van pressed on to assault the South Side Gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiu Fan reached Xinting, the Great Bridge was abandoned, and his vanguard pressed on to attack the South Side Gate of the palace.

sentences.zh: 永遣人覘賊，既返，唱云：「臺城陷矣。

translations.literal: Yong sent men to reconnoiter the rebels; when they returned, they cried aloud: "The palace city has fallen."
translations.idiomatic: Yong sent men to scout the rebels; when they returned, they shouted aloud: "The palace city has fallen!"

sentences.zh: 」永眾於此潰散，永亦棄軍奔走，還先所住南苑。

translations.literal: At this Yong's troops broke and scattered; Yong too abandoned his army and fled, returning to the Southern Park where he had lodged before.
translations.idiomatic: At this Yong's troops broke and fled. Yong too abandoned his army and ran, retreating to the Southern Park where he had lodged before.

sentences.zh: 以永舊臣不加罪，止免官削爵，永亦愧歎發病。

translations.literal: Because Yong was an old minister he was not punished; he was only dismissed from office and stripped of his title. Yong also fell ill from shame and sighing.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yong was a veteran minister he was not punished further—only dismissed and stripped of his title. Yong, shamed and despairing, fell ill.

sentences.zh: 三年，卒，時年六十六。

translations.literal: In the third year he died, aged sixty-six.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he died, at the age of sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 順帝昇明二年，追贈侍中、右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shengming under Emperor Shun, he was posthumously granted Palace Attendant and Right Grand Master of Glorious Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shengming under Emperor Shun, he was posthumously granted Palace Attendant and Right Grand Master of Glorious Happiness.

sentences.zh: 子瑰，昇明末，達官。

translations.literal: His son Gui, at the end of Shengming, reached high office.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gui reached high office at the end of the Shengming era.

sentences.zh: 永弟辯，太宗亦見任遇，歷尚書吏部郎，廣州刺史，大司農。

translations.literal: Yong's younger brother Bian was also favored and employed under Taizong; he served as Director in the Ministry of Personnel under the Secretariat, Inspector of Guangzhou, and Grand Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: Yong's younger brother Bian was also favored under Taizong, serving as Director in the Ministry of Personnel, Inspector of Guangzhou, and Grand Minister of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 辯弟岱，昇明末，吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Bian's younger brother Dai, at the end of Shengming, was Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Bian's younger brother Dai became Minister of Personnel at the end of the Shengming era.

sentences.zh: 庾登之

translations.literal: Yu Dengzhi
translations.idiomatic: Yu Dengzhi

sentences.zh: 庾登之，字元龍，潁川鄢陵人也。

translations.literal: Yu Dengzhi, courtesy name Yuanlong, was a native of Yanling in Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Dengzhi, courtesy name Yuanlong, was a native of Yanling in Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 曾祖冰，晉司空。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Bing was Minister of Works under Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Bing had been Minister of Works under Jin.

sentences.zh: 祖蘊，廣州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yun was Inspector of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yun had been Inspector of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 父廓，東陽太守。

translations.literal: His father Kuo was Administrator of Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kuo had been Administrator of Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 登之少以強濟自立，初為晉會稽王道子太傅參軍。

translations.literal: Dengzhi in youth relied on forceful capability to establish himself; he first served as Aide to the Grand Tutor of Prince of Kuaiji Daozi under Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Dengzhi established himself in youth through forceful capability. He first served as aide to the Grand Tutor of Prince of Kuaiji Daozi under Jin.

sentences.zh: 義旗初，又為高祖鎮軍參軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Righteous Banner he again served as Aide on Gaozu's Suppressing Army staff.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Righteous Banner uprising he again served as aide on Gaozu's Suppressing Army staff.

sentences.zh: 以預討桓玄功，封曲江縣五等男。

translations.literal: For participating in the campaign against Huan Xuan he was enfeoffed as Fifth-rank Baron of Qujiang.
translations.idiomatic: For taking part in the campaign against Huan Xuan he was enfeoffed as Fifth-rank Baron of Qujiang.

sentences.zh: 參大司馬琅邪王軍事，豫州別駕從事史，大司馬主簿，司徒左西曹屬。

translations.literal: He served as aide on the Grand Marshal's staff of the Prince of Langya, Attendant Officer on the Registrar's staff of Yuzhou, Chief Clerk to the Grand Marshal, and Aide in the Left Western Section of the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He served on the Grand Marshal's staff of the Prince of Langya, as Attendant Officer on the Registrar's staff of Yuzhou, as Chief Clerk to the Grand Marshal, and as Aide in the Left Western Section of the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 登之雖不涉學，善於世事，王弘、謝晦、江夷之徒，皆相知友。

translations.literal: Though Dengzhi was not versed in learning, he was skilled in worldly affairs, and Wang Hong, Xie Hui, Jiang Yi, and others were all his friends.
translations.idiomatic: Though Dengzhi was not a scholar, he was skilled in practical affairs, and Wang Hong, Xie Hui, Jiang Yi, and others counted him as a friend.

sentences.zh: 轉太尉主簿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Chief Clerk to the Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Chief Clerk to the Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 義熙十二年，高祖北伐，登之擊節驅馳，退告劉穆之，以母老求郡。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Yixi, when Gaozu marched north, Dengzhi drove hard at the drum's beat; then he withdrew and reported to Liu Muzhi, asking for a commandery post because his mother was old.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Yixi, when Gaozu marched north, Dengzhi drove hard at the drum's beat, then withdrew and reported to Liu Muzhi, asking for a commandery post because his mother was old.

sentences.zh: 於是士庶咸憚遠役，而登之二三其心，高祖大怒，除吏名。

translations.literal: At that time officials and commoners alike dreaded long-range service, yet Dengzhi wavered in his resolve; Gaozu was furious and struck his name from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: At a time when officials and commoners alike dreaded distant service, Dengzhi wavered in his commitment. Gaozu was furious and struck his name from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 大軍發後，乃以補鎮蠻護軍、西陽太守。

translations.literal: After the main army had set out, he was appointed in his place as Protector General of the Barbarian Pacification and Administrator of Xiyang.
translations.idiomatic: After the main army had set out, he was appointed Protector General of the Barbarian Pacification and Administrator of Xiyang.

sentences.zh: 入為太子庶子，尚書左丞。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Vice Tutor to the Crown Prince and Senior Assistant in the Ministry of Works under the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as Vice Tutor to the Crown Prince and Senior Assistant in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 出為新安太守。

translations.literal: He went out as Administrator of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Administrator of Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 謝晦為撫軍將軍、荊州刺史，請為長史、南郡太守，仍為衛軍長史，太守如故。

translations.literal: When Xie Hui was made General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Jingzhou, he requested Dengzhi as Chief Administrator and Administrator of Nan Commandery; Dengzhi later served as Chief Administrator on the Guard Army staff, retaining his post as Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: When Xie Hui became General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Jingzhou, he asked for Dengzhi as his Chief Administrator and Administrator of Nan Commandery. Dengzhi later served as Chief Administrator on the Guard Army staff while retaining his post as Administrator.

sentences.zh: 登之與晦俱曹氏婿，名位本同，一旦為之佐，意甚不愜。

translations.literal: Dengzhi and Hui were both sons-in-law of the Cao family and had originally been equals in rank; suddenly to serve as his assistant left him very discontented.
translations.idiomatic: Dengzhi and Hui were both sons-in-law of the Cao family and had originally been equals in rank. To serve suddenly as Hui's subordinate left Dengzhi deeply discontented.

sentences.zh: 到廳牋，唯云「即日恭到」，初無感謝之言。

translations.literal: When he arrived at the office and submitted his memorial, he wrote only "Respectfully arrived this day," with no words of gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived at headquarters and submitted his arrival memorial, he wrote only "Respectfully arrived this day," with no word of thanks.

sentences.zh: 每入覲見，備持箱囊几席之屬，一物不具不坐。

translations.literal: Whenever he went in for an audience he brought with him chests, bags, tables, and mats; if a single item was missing he would not sit.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he went in for an audience he brought his own chests, bags, tables, and mats; if a single item was missing he would not sit down.

sentences.zh: 晦常優容之。

translations.literal: Hui often indulged him.
translations.idiomatic: Hui often indulged him.

sentences.zh: 晦拒王師，欲使登之留守，登之不許，語在晦傳。

translations.literal: When Hui resisted the imperial army he wanted Dengzhi to remain and hold the fort; Dengzhi refused—the account is in Hui's biography.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui resisted the imperial army he wanted Dengzhi to remain and hold the fort, but Dengzhi refused—the account is given in Hui's biography.

sentences.zh: 晦敗，登之以無任免罪，禁錮還家。

translations.literal: When Hui was defeated, Dengzhi was punished for inaction and confined, then sent home.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui was defeated, Dengzhi was punished for failing to act and was confined and sent home.

sentences.zh: 元嘉五年，起為衡陽王義季征虜長史。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yuanjia he was recalled as Chief Administrator on Prince of Hengyang Yiji's Campaign Army staff.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Yuanjia he was recalled as Chief Administrator on Prince of Hengyang Yiji's Campaign Army staff.

sentences.zh: 義季年少，未親政，眾事一以委之。

translations.literal: Yiji was young and did not personally attend to administration; all affairs were entirely entrusted to Dengzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Yiji was young and did not personally attend to government; all affairs were entrusted entirely to Dengzhi.

sentences.zh: 尋加南東海太守。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally made Administrator of South Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was additionally appointed Administrator of South Donghai.

sentences.zh: 入為司徒右長史，尚書吏部郎，司徒左長史，南東海太守。

translations.literal: He entered as Senior Administrator on the Right of the Minister of Education, Director in the Ministry of Personnel under the Secretariat, Senior Administrator on the Left of the Minister of Education, and Administrator of South Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as Senior Administrator on the Right of the Minister of Education, Director in the Ministry of Personnel, Senior Administrator on the Left of the Minister of Education, and Administrator of South Donghai.

sentences.zh: 府公彭城王義康專覽政事，不欲自下厝懷，而登之性剛，每陳己意，義康甚不悅，出為吳郡太守。

translations.literal: The Prince of Pengcheng Yikang, head of the office, monopolized affairs of government and did not wish to condescend to receive others' concerns; but Dengzhi was stiff by nature and often stated his own views, which greatly displeased Yikang, and he was sent out as Administrator of Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Pengcheng Yikang, head of the office, monopolized government affairs and did not wish to hear subordinates' views. Dengzhi was stiff by nature and often stated his own opinions, which greatly displeased Yikang, and Dengzhi was sent out as Administrator of Wu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 州郡相臨，執意無改，因其蒞任贓貨，以事免官。

translations.literal: The two provinces adjoined each other; Dengzhi's obstinacy was unchanged, and on charges of corruption during Yikang's tenure he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: The two provinces adjoined each other, and Dengzhi's obstinacy was unchanged. On charges of corruption during Yikang's tenure he was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 弟炳之時為臨川內史，登之隨弟之郡，優遊自適。

translations.literal: His younger brother Bingzhi was then Administrator of Linchuan; Dengzhi followed his brother to the commandery and lived at ease in leisure.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Bingzhi was then Administrator of Linchuan, and Dengzhi followed him to the commandery, living at ease.

sentences.zh: 俄而除豫章太守，便道之官。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Administrator of Yuzhang and proceeded to his post by the direct route.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed Administrator of Yuzhang and proceeded directly to his post.

sentences.zh: 登之初至臨川，吏民咸相輕侮，豫章與臨川接境，郡又華大，儀迓光赫，土人並驚歎焉。

translations.literal: When Dengzhi first arrived at Linchuan, officials and people all slighted and insulted him; Yuzhang bordered Linchuan, and that commandery was both splendid and great—when Dengzhi's ceremonial reception blazed in splendor, the local people were all astonished.
translations.idiomatic: When Dengzhi first arrived at Linchuan, officials and people had all slighted him. Yuzhang bordered Linchuan and was a splendid, great commandery; when Dengzhi's ceremonial reception blazed in splendor, the local people were astonished.

sentences.zh: 十八年，遷江州刺史。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was transferred to Inspector of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was transferred to Inspector of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 疾篤，徵為中護軍。

translations.literal: When his illness grew grave he was summoned as Chief of the Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When his illness grew grave he was summoned as Chief of the Palace Guard.

sentences.zh: 未拜。

translations.literal: He did not assume the post.
translations.idiomatic: He did not assume the post.

sentences.zh: 二十年，卒，時年六十二。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he died, aged sixty-two.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he died, at the age of sixty-two.

sentences.zh: 即以為贈。

translations.literal: The post to which he had been summoned was granted posthumously.
translations.idiomatic: The post to which he had been summoned was granted posthumously.

sentences.zh: 子沖遠，太宗鎮姑孰，為衛軍長史，卒於豫章太守，追贈侍中。

translations.literal: His son Chongyuan, when Taizong garrisoned Gushu, served as Chief Administrator on the Guard Army staff; he died while Administrator of Yuzhang and was posthumously granted Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chongyuan, when Taizong garrisoned Gushu, served as Chief Administrator on the Guard Army staff. He died while Administrator of Yuzhang and was posthumously granted Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 弟炳之

translations.literal: (Younger brother Bingzhi)
translations.idiomatic: (Younger brother Bingzhi)

sentences.zh: 炳之，字仲文，初為秘書、太子舍人，劉粹征北長史、廣平太守。

translations.literal: Bingzhi, courtesy name Zhongwen, first served as Secretary and Staff Officer to the Crown Prince, then as Chief Administrator on Liu Cui's North Conquest Army staff and Administrator of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: Bingzhi, courtesy name Zhongwen, first served as Secretary and Staff Officer to the Crown Prince, then as Chief Administrator on Liu Cui's North Conquest Army staff and Administrator of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 兄登之為謝晦長史，炳之往省之。

translations.literal: When his elder brother Dengzhi was Chief Administrator to Xie Hui, Bingzhi went to visit him.
translations.idiomatic: When his elder brother Dengzhi was Chief Administrator to Xie Hui, Bingzhi went to visit him.

sentences.zh: 晦時位高權重，朝士莫不加敬，炳之獨與抗禮，時論健之。

translations.literal: Hui then held high rank and great power; not one court official failed to show him extra deference, but Bingzhi alone treated him as an equal—opinion at the time praised his boldness.
translations.idiomatic: Hui then held high rank and great power, and every court official showed him extra deference. Bingzhi alone treated him as an equal, and opinion at the time praised his boldness.

sentences.zh: 為尚書度支郎，不拜。

translations.literal: He was appointed Director of Revenue in the Ministry of Works under the Secretariat but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Director of Revenue in the Ministry of Works but did not accept the post.

sentences.zh: 出補錢塘令，治民有績。

translations.literal: He went out to fill the post of Magistrate of Qiantang and governed the people with achievement.
translations.idiomatic: He went out to serve as Magistrate of Qiantang and governed the people with distinction.

sentences.zh: 轉彭城王義康驃騎主簿，未就，徙為丹陽丞。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Chief Clerk on Prince of Pengcheng Yikang's Swift Cavalry staff; before he took up the post he was moved to Assistant Administrator of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Chief Clerk on Prince of Pengcheng Yikang's Swift Cavalry staff, but before he took up the post he was moved to Assistant Administrator of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 炳之既未到府，疑於府公禮敬，下禮官博議。

translations.literal: Since Bingzhi had not yet reached the prince's office, he was uncertain about the courtesies owed the prince's household and submitted the question for broad deliberation by the ritual officials.
translations.idiomatic: Since Bingzhi had not yet reached the prince's headquarters, he was uncertain about the courtesies owed the prince's household and submitted the question for broad deliberation by the ritual officials.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎裴松之議曰：「案《春秋》桓八年，祭公逆王后于紀。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Pei Songzhi submitted an opinion: "Examining the Spring and Autumn Annals, Duke Huan's eighth year: Duke Ji met the queen in Ji."
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Pei Songzhi submitted an opinion: "Examining the Spring and Autumn Annals, in Duke Huan's eighth year Duke Ji met the queen in Ji."

sentences.zh: 《公羊傳》曰：『女在國稱女，此其稱王后何？

translations.literal: The Gongyang Commentary says: 'An unmarried woman in her state is called nǚ; why is she here called queen?'
translations.idiomatic: The Gongyang Commentary says: 'An unmarried woman in her state is called nǚ; why is she here called queen?'

sentences.zh: 王者無外，其辭成矣。

translations.literal: The king has no outside—thereby the designation is complete.'
translations.idiomatic: The king has no outside—thereby the designation is complete.'

sentences.zh: 』推此而言，則炳之為吏之道，定於受命之日矣，其辭已成，在官無外，名器既正，則禮亦從之。

translations.literal: Applying this principle, Bingzhi's status as an official was fixed from the day he received his appointment: the designation was already complete; once in office there is no 'outside'; when title and office are correct, ritual follows accordingly."
translations.idiomatic: Applying this principle, Bingzhi's status as an official was fixed from the day he received his appointment: the designation was already complete; once in office there is no 'outside'; when title and office are correct, ritual follows accordingly."

sentences.zh: 且今宰牧之官，拜不之職，未接之民，必有其敬者，以既受王命，則成君民之義故也。

translations.literal: Moreover, among magistrates and governors today, those who accept appointment but do not yet take up their posts—among the people they have not yet met there are inevitably those who show them respect, because once they have received the royal mandate the lord-and-subject bond is complete.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, among magistrates and governors today, those who accept appointment but have not yet taken up their posts will find people they have never met showing them respect, because once they have received the royal mandate the bond between lord and subject is complete.

sentences.zh: 吏之被敕，猶除者受拜，民不以未見闕其被禮，吏安可以未到廢其節乎？

translations.literal: An official who receives an edict of appointment is like one who receives investiture: the people do not withhold the rites of respect because they have not yet seen him—how can an official abandon his ritual obligations merely because he has not yet arrived?
translations.idiomatic: An official who receives an edict of appointment is like one who receives investiture: the people do not withhold the rites of respect because they have not yet seen him—how can an official abandon his ritual obligations merely because he has not yet arrived?

sentences.zh: 愚懷所見，宜執吏禮。

translations.literal: In my humble view, he should observe the rites due an official.
translations.idiomatic: In my humble view, he should observe the rites due an official.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: His opinion was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: His opinion was adopted.

sentences.zh: 遷司徒左西屬。

translations.literal: Bingzhi was transferred to Aide in the Left Western Section of the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Bingzhi was transferred to Aide in the Left Western Section of the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 左將軍竟陵王義宣未親府，板炳之為諮議參軍，眾務悉委焉。

translations.literal: Left General Prince of Jingling Yixuan did not personally attend to his headquarters; Bingzhi was appointed Consulting Army Aide on his staff, and all affairs were entirely entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Left General Prince of Jingling Yixuan did not personally attend to his headquarters. Bingzhi was appointed Consulting Army Aide on his staff, and all affairs were entrusted entirely to him.

sentences.zh: 後將軍長沙王義欣鎮壽陽，炳之為長史、南梁郡太守，轉鎮國長史，太守如故。

translations.literal: Rear General Prince of Changsha Yixin garrisoned Shouyang; Bingzhi served as Chief Administrator and Administrator of South Liang Commandery, then was transferred to Chief Administrator on the Pacifying the State staff, retaining his post as Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Rear General Prince of Changsha Yixin garrisoned Shouyang. Bingzhi served as Chief Administrator and Administrator of South Liang Commandery, then was transferred to Chief Administrator on the Pacifying the State staff while retaining his post as Administrator.

sentences.zh: 出為臨川內史。

translations.literal: He went out as Administrator of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Administrator of Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 後將軍始興王濬鎮湘州，以炳之為司馬，領長沙內史。

translations.literal: Rear General Prince of Shixing Jun garrisoned Xiangzhou; Bingzhi was appointed Chief Administrator and concurrently Administrator of Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Rear General Prince of Shixing Jun garrisoned Xiangzhou and appointed Bingzhi Chief Administrator and concurrently Administrator of Changsha.

sentences.zh: 濬不之任，除南太山太守，司馬如故。

translations.literal: Jun did not go to his post; Bingzhi was appointed Administrator of South Taishan while retaining his post as Chief Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Jun did not go to his post. Bingzhi was appointed Administrator of South Taishan while retaining his post as Chief Administrator.

sentences.zh: 于時領軍將軍劉湛協附大將軍彭城王義康，而與僕射殷景仁有隙，凡朝士游殷氏者，不得入劉氏之門，獨炳之遊二人之間，密盡忠於朝廷。

translations.literal: At that time Palace Guard General Liu Zhan attached himself to Grand General Prince of Pengcheng Yikang, yet was at odds with Vice Director Yin Jingren; any court official who associated with the Yin clan could not enter the Liu clan's gate—Bingzhi alone moved between the two camps, secretly giving his full loyalty to the court.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Palace Guard General Liu Zhan attached himself to Grand General Prince of Pengcheng Yikang but was at odds with Vice Director Yin Jingren. Any court official who associated with the Yin clan could not enter the Liu clan's gate—Bingzhi alone moved between the two camps, secretly giving his full loyalty to the court.

sentences.zh: 景仁稱疾不朝見者歷年，太祖常令炳之銜命去來，湛不疑也。

translations.literal: Jingren feigned illness and did not attend court for years; Taizu often sent Bingzhi back and forth bearing orders, and Zhan suspected nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Jingren feigned illness and did not attend court for years. Taizu often sent Bingzhi back and forth bearing orders, and Zhan suspected nothing.

sentences.zh: 義康出藩，湛伏誅，以炳之為尚書吏部郎，與右衛將軍沈演之俱參機密。

translations.literal: When Yikang was sent out to his fief and Zhan was executed, Bingzhi was appointed Director in the Ministry of Personnel under the Secretariat and, with Right Guard General Shen Yanzhi, jointly handled secret affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: When Yikang was sent out to his fief and Zhan was executed, Bingzhi was appointed Director in the Ministry of Personnel and, with Right Guard General Shen Yanzhi, jointly handled secret affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 頃之，轉侍中，本州大中正。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Palace Attendant and Chief Rectifier of his native province.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to Palace Attendant and Chief Rectifier of his native province.

sentences.zh: 遷吏部尚書，領義陽王師。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Personnel and appointed Preceptor to the Prince of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Minister of Personnel and appointed Preceptor to the Prince of Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 內外歸附，勢傾朝野。

translations.literal: Within and without the court, men rallied to him; his power overshadowed the court and countryside.
translations.idiomatic: Within and without the court, men rallied to him, and his power overshadowed court and countryside.

sentences.zh: 炳之為人彊急而不耐煩，賓客干訴非理者，忿詈形於辭色。

translations.literal: Bingzhi was forceful and impatient by nature; when guests petitioned him unreasonably, anger and curses showed plainly in his words and face.
translations.idiomatic: Bingzhi was forceful and impatient by nature. When guests petitioned him unreasonably, anger and curses showed plainly in his words and face.

sentences.zh: 素無術學，不為眾望所推。

translations.literal: He had never possessed learning, and was not favored by public expectation.
translations.idiomatic: He had never possessed learning and was not favored by public expectation.

sentences.zh: 性好潔，士大夫造之者，去未出戶，輒令人拭席洗床。

translations.literal: He was fastidiously clean by nature; when gentry visitors left, before they had even passed the door he would have someone wipe the mat and wash the couch.
translations.idiomatic: He was fastidiously clean by nature. When gentry visitors left, before they had even passed the door he would have someone wipe the mat and wash the couch.

sentences.zh: 時陳郡殷沖亦好淨，小史非淨浴新衣，不得近左右。

translations.literal: At the time Yin Chong of Chen Commandery also loved cleanliness; lesser clerks who had not bathed clean and donned fresh clothes could not approach his side.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Yin Chong of Chen Commandery also loved cleanliness. Lesser clerks who had not bathed clean and donned fresh clothes could not approach his side.

sentences.zh: 士大夫小不整潔，每容接之。

translations.literal: Even when gentry were slightly untidy, he would still receive them.
translations.idiomatic: Even when gentry were slightly untidy, he would still receive them.

sentences.zh: 炳之好潔反是，沖每以此譏焉。

translations.literal: Bingzhi's fastidiousness was the opposite; Yin Chong often mocked him for it.
translations.idiomatic: Bingzhi's fastidiousness was the opposite, and Yin Chong often mocked him for it.

sentences.zh: 領選既不緝眾論，又頗通貨賄。

translations.literal: As head of selection he neither reconciled public opinion nor refrained from trafficking in bribes.
translations.idiomatic: As head of selection he neither reconciled public opinion nor refrained from trafficking in bribes.

sentences.zh: 炳之請急還家，吏部令史錢泰、主客令史周伯齊出炳之宅咨事。

translations.literal: Bingzhi requested urgent leave to return home; Clerks of the Ministry of Personnel Qian Tai and Guest Affairs Clerk Zhou Boqi came to Bingzhi's residence on official business.
translations.idiomatic: Bingzhi requested urgent leave to return home. Ministry of Personnel Clerk Qian Tai and Guest Affairs Clerk Zhou Boqi came to Bingzhi's residence on official business.

sentences.zh: 泰能彈琵琶，伯齊善歌，炳之因留停宿。

translations.literal: Tai could play the pipa and Boqi was skilled at song; Bingzhi therefore kept them overnight.
translations.idiomatic: Tai could play the pipa and Boqi was skilled at song, so Bingzhi kept them overnight.

sentences.zh: 尚書舊制，令史咨事，不得宿停外，雖有八座命，亦不許。

translations.literal: Under the old regulations of the Secretariat, when clerks came on official consultation they were not permitted to stay overnight outside the office—even on orders from the eight chief ministers this was forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old regulations of the Secretariat, when clerks came on official consultation they were not permitted to stay overnight outside the office—even on orders from the eight chief ministers this was forbidden.

sentences.zh: 為有司所奏。

translations.literal: He was reported by the relevant officials.
translations.idiomatic: He was reported by the relevant officials.

sentences.zh: 上於炳之素厚，將恕之，召問尚書右僕射何尚之，尚之具陳炳之得失。

translations.literal: The sovereign had long been close to Bingzhi and was about to pardon him. He summoned Vice Director of the Secretariat He Shangzhi and questioned him; Shangzhi fully stated Bingzhi's faults and merits.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign had long been close to Bingzhi and was about to pardon him. He summoned Vice Director of the Secretariat He Shangzhi and questioned him, and Shangzhi fully stated Bingzhi's faults and merits.

sentences.zh: 又密奏曰：「夫為國為家，何嘗不謹用前典，今苟欲通一人，慮非哲王御世之長術。

translations.literal: He also submitted a secret memorial saying: "In governing state and family, when has one ever failed to carefully follow precedent? If now you wish merely to let one man through, I fear that is not the sage king's long method for governing the age."
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted a secret memorial saying: "In governing state and family, when has one ever failed to carefully follow precedent? If Your Majesty now wishes merely to let one man through, I fear that is not the sage king's long method for governing the age."

sentences.zh: 炳之所行，非曖昧而已。

translations.literal: Bingzhi's conduct is not merely ambiguous.
translations.idiomatic: Bingzhi's conduct is not merely ambiguous.

sentences.zh: 臣所聞既非一旦，又往往眼見，事如丘山，彰彰若此，遂縱而不糾，不知復何以為治。

translations.literal: What your servant has heard was not accumulated in a single day; I have often seen it with my own eyes. The matter is mountain-high—so glaringly obvious. Yet he is indulged and not punished. I know not by what further means governance can be carried on.
translations.idiomatic: What I have heard was not accumulated in a single day, and I have often seen it with my own eyes. The matter is mountain-high and glaringly obvious, yet he is indulged and not punished. I know not by what further means governance can be carried on.

sentences.zh: 晉武不曰明主，斷鬲令事，遂能奮發，華暠見待不輕，廢錮累年，後起，止作城門校尉耳。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Jin cannot be called an enlightened ruler, yet in the Ge Ling affair he was able to rouse himself to action. Hua Gao had been treated with no small consideration, yet was confined and banned for years; when he was later recalled, he held only the post of Gate Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Jin cannot be called an enlightened ruler, yet in the Ge Ling affair he was able to rouse himself to action. Hua Gao had been treated with no small consideration, yet was confined and banned for years; when he was later recalled, he held only the post of Gate Commandant.

sentences.zh: 若言炳之有誠於國，未知的是何事？

translations.literal: If one says Bingzhi has shown sincerity toward the state, I know not what exactly that would be.
translations.idiomatic: If one says Bingzhi has shown sincerity toward the state, I know not what exactly that would be.

sentences.zh: 政當云與殷景仁不失其舊，與劉湛亦復不疏。

translations.literal: One might as well say that with Yin Jingren he maintained the old closeness and with Liu Zhan he was again not estranged.
translations.idiomatic: One might as well say that with Yin Jingren he maintained their old closeness and with Liu Zhan he was again not estranged.

sentences.zh: 且景仁當時事意，豈復可蔑，朝士兩邊相推，亦復何限，縱有微誠，復何足掩其惡。

translations.literal: Moreover, can Jingren's role in the affairs of that time truly be dismissed? Court officials pushing one another between the two factions were again without limit. Even if there were slight sincerity, how could it suffice to cover his wickedness?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, can Jingren's role in the affairs of that time truly be dismissed? Court officials pushing one another between the two factions were without limit. Even if there were slight sincerity, how could it suffice to cover his wickedness?

sentences.zh: 今賈充勳烈，晉之重臣，雖事業不勝，不聞有大罪，諸臣進說，便遠出之。

translations.literal: Now Jia Chong's meritorious achievements made him a chief minister of Jin. Although his accomplishments did not measure up, one never heard of great crimes; yet when the ministers urged it, he was sent far away.
translations.idiomatic: Now Jia Chong's meritorious achievements made him a chief minister of Jin. Although his accomplishments did not measure up, one never heard of great crimes, yet when the ministers urged it, he was sent far away.

sentences.zh: 陛下聖叡，反更遲遲於此。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is sage and perceptive, yet you are all the more slow in this.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is sage and perceptive, yet you are all the more slow in this.

sentences.zh: 炳之身上之釁，既自藉藉，交結朋黨，構扇是非，實足亂俗傷風。

translations.literal: The offenses on Bingzhi's own person are already notorious. He forms factions and cliques, stirs up right and wrong—more than enough to corrupt customs and harm the age.
translations.idiomatic: The offenses on Bingzhi's own person are already notorious. He forms factions and cliques, stirs up right and wrong—more than enough to corrupt customs and harm the age.

sentences.zh: 諸惡紛紜，過於范曄，所少賊一事耳。

translations.literal: The various wicked deeds are confused and manifold, exceeding Fan Ye—he lacks only the one crime of treason.
translations.idiomatic: The various wicked deeds are confused and manifold, exceeding Fan Ye—he lacks only the one crime of treason.

sentences.zh: 伏願深加三思，試以諸聲傳，普訪諸可顧問者。

translations.literal: I humbly wish Your Majesty would deeply reconsider thrice, and try to follow the various rumors, broadly inquiring of all who may be consulted.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly wish Your Majesty would deeply reconsider thrice, try to follow the various rumors, and broadly inquire of all who may be consulted.

sentences.zh: 群下見陛下顧遇既重，恐不敢苦相侵傷；

translations.literal: When the ranks below see that Your Majesty's gracious treatment of Bingzhi is already weighty, I fear they will not dare to press the injury harshly;
translations.idiomatic: When the ranks below see that Your Majesty's gracious treatment of Bingzhi is already weighty, I fear they will not dare to press the injury harshly;

sentences.zh: 顧問之日，宜布嫌責之旨。

translations.literal: On the day of inquiry, it would be fitting to proclaim your intent of distrust and censure.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of inquiry, it would be fitting to proclaim your intent of distrust and censure.

sentences.zh: 若不如此，亦當不辯有所得失。

translations.literal: If it is not thus, one will likewise be unable to distinguish whether there is gain or loss.
translations.idiomatic: If it is not thus, one will likewise be unable to distinguish whether there is gain or loss.

sentences.zh: 臣蠢，既有所啟，要欲盡其心，如無可納，伏願宥其觸忤之罪。」

translations.literal: Your servant is dull. Since I have made this appeal, I must wish to exhaust my heart. If there is nothing to be accepted, I humbly pray you pardon the crime of having offended."
translations.idiomatic: Your servant is dull. Since I have made this appeal, I must wish to exhaust my heart. If there is nothing to be accepted, I humbly pray you pardon the crime of having offended."

sentences.zh: 時炳之自理：「不諳臺制，令史並言停外非嫌。

translations.literal: At the time Bingzhi explained in his own defense: "I was unfamiliar with the regulations of the Secretariat; the clerks both said that overnight lodging outside involved no offense."
translations.idiomatic: At the time Bingzhi explained in his own defense: "I was unfamiliar with the regulations of the Secretariat; the clerks both said that overnight lodging outside involved no offense."

sentences.zh: 」太祖以炳之信受失所，小事不足傷大臣。

translations.literal: Taizu considered that Bingzhi had merely failed to receive and trust properly—a small matter, not enough to injure a great minister.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu considered that Bingzhi had merely failed to receive and trust properly—a small matter, not enough to injure a great minister.

sentences.zh: 尚之又陳曰：「炳之呼二令史出宿，令史諮都令史駱宰，宰云不通，吏部曹亦咸知不可，令史具向炳之說不得停之意，炳之了不聽納。

translations.literal: Shangzhi again submitted, saying: "Bingzhi called the two clerks out to lodge overnight. The clerks consulted Chief Clerk Luo Zai; Zai said it was impermissible. The Ministry of Personnel section also all knew it could not be done. The clerks fully explained to Bingzhi the meaning of why overnight lodging was forbidden, yet Bingzhi completely refused to accept it."
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhi again submitted, saying: "Bingzhi called the two clerks out to lodge overnight. The clerks consulted Chief Clerk Luo Zai; Zai said it was impermissible. The Ministry of Personnel section also all knew it could not be done. The clerks fully explained to Bingzhi why overnight lodging was forbidden, yet Bingzhi completely refused to accept it."

sentences.zh: 此非為不解，直是苟相留耳。

translations.literal: This was not because he did not understand—it was simply that he wanted to keep them on by any means.
translations.idiomatic: This was not because he did not understand—it was simply that he wanted to keep them on by any means.

sentences.zh: 由外悉知此，而誣於信受，群情豈了，陛下不假為之辭。
