translations.literal: The outside all knew this, yet he pretends it was a failure of trust and receipt—how could public sentiment be satisfied? Your Majesty need not make excuses for him.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone outside knew this, yet he pretends it was a failure of trust and receipt—how could public sentiment be satisfied? Your Majesty need not make excuses for him.

sentences.zh: 雖是令史，出乃遠虧朝典，又不得謂之小事。

translations.literal: Although they were mere clerks, allowing them out grossly violated court precedent, and this cannot be called a small matter.
translations.idiomatic: Although they were mere clerks, allowing them out grossly violated court precedent, and this cannot be called a small matter.

sentences.zh: 謝晦望實，非今者之疇，一事錯誤，免侍中官。

translations.literal: Xie Hui's reputation and accomplishment were not in the same category as today's case; one mistaken affair cost him his post as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Hui's reputation and accomplishment were not in the same category as today's case; one mistaken affair cost him his post as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 王珣時賢小失，桓胤春蒐之謬，皆白衣領職。

translations.literal: Wang Xun, a man of talent, suffered a small fault; Huan Yin's error at the spring hunt—both served their posts in plain clothes.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xun, a man of talent, suffered a small fault; Huan Yin's error at the spring hunt—both served their posts in plain clothes.

sentences.zh: 況公犯憲制者邪？

translations.literal: How much more when a public servant violates statutes and regulations?
translations.idiomatic: How much more when a public servant violates statutes and regulations?

sentences.zh: 不審可有同王、桓白衣例不？

translations.literal: I know not whether there exists a precedent, like Wang and Huan, of serving in plain clothes?
translations.idiomatic: I know not whether there exists a precedent, like Wang and Huan, of serving in plain clothes?

sentences.zh: 於任使無損，兼可得以為肅戒。

translations.literal: It would not harm his employment and appointment, and would also serve as a disciplinary warning.
translations.idiomatic: It would not harm his employment and appointment, and would also serve as a disciplinary warning.

sentences.zh: 孔萬祀居左丞之局，不念相當，語駱宰云：『炳之貴要，異他尚書身，政可得無言耳。

translations.literal: Kong Wansi held the post of Left Assistant Director yet gave no thought to propriety. He told Luo Zai: 'Bingzhi is lofty and influential, unlike other ministers of the Secretariat; one really can say nothing about him.'
translations.idiomatic: Kong Wansi held the post of Left Assistant Director yet gave no thought to propriety. He told Luo Zai: 'Bingzhi is lofty and influential, unlike other ministers of the Secretariat; one really can say nothing about him.'

sentences.zh: 』又云：『不癡不聾，不成姑公。

translations.literal: He also said: 'Without being foolish or deaf, one cannot be an aunt-mother-in-law.'
translations.idiomatic: He also said: 'Without being foolish or deaf, one cannot be an aunt-mother-in-law.'

sentences.zh: 』敢作此言，亦為異也。」

translations.literal: To dare speak such words is also extraordinary."
translations.idiomatic: To dare speak such words is also extraordinary."

sentences.zh: 太祖猶優游之，使尚之更陳其意。

translations.literal: Taizu still treated the matter leniently and had Shangzhi state his views again.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu still treated the matter leniently and had Shangzhi state his views again.

sentences.zh: 尚之乃備言炳之愆過，曰：「尚書舊有增置幹二十人，以元、凱丞郎幹之假疾病，炳之常取十人私使，詢處幹闕，不得時補。

translations.literal: Shangzhi then fully stated Bingzhi's faults and offenses, saying: "The Secretariat formerly had twenty additional clerks appointed. Clerks Yuan and Kai feigned illness; Bingzhi regularly took ten for his private use. When I inquired, the posts of the clerks were vacant and could not be filled in time."
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhi then fully stated Bingzhi's faults and offenses, saying: "The Secretariat formerly had twenty additional clerks appointed. Clerks Yuan and Kai feigned illness; Bingzhi regularly took ten for his private use. When I inquired, the posts of the clerks were vacant and could not be filled in time."

sentences.zh: 近得王師，猶不遣還，臣令人語之，『先取人使，意常未安，今既有手力，不宜復留。

translations.literal: Recently when the army returned in victory he still would not send them back. I had someone tell him, 'First you took men for your use—I have always felt uneasy about this. Now that you have your own servants, they should not be kept anymore.'
translations.idiomatic: Recently when the army returned in victory he still would not send them back. I had someone tell him, 'First you took men for your use—I have always felt uneasy about this. Now that you have your own servants, they should not be kept anymore.'

sentences.zh: 』得臣此信，方復遣耳。

translations.literal: Only upon receiving this letter of mine did he finally send them back.
translations.idiomatic: Only upon receiving this letter of mine did he finally send them back.

sentences.zh: 大都為人好率懷行事，有諸紜紜，不悉可曉。

translations.literal: Generally he is the sort of man who acts from impulse and favor in all things; there are many confused matters that cannot all be understood.
translations.idiomatic: Generally he is the sort of man who acts from impulse and favor in all things; there are many confused matters that cannot all be understood.

sentences.zh: 臣思張遼之言，關羽雖兄弟，曹公父子，豈得不言。

translations.literal: I think of Zhang Liao's words—even though Guan Yu was a sworn brother and Cao Cao father and son, could one fail to speak?
translations.idiomatic: I think of Zhang Liao's words—even though Guan Yu was a sworn brother and Cao Cao father and son, could one fail to speak?

sentences.zh: 觀今人憂國實寡，臣復結舌，日月之明，或有所蔽。

translations.literal: Looking at men today, there are truly few who worry for the state. Your servant again holds his tongue; the sun and moon's brightness may in places be obscured.
translations.idiomatic: Looking at men today, there are truly few who worry for the state. Your servant again holds his tongue; the sun and moon's brightness may in places be obscured.

sentences.zh: 然不知臣者，豈不謂臣有爭競之跡，追以悵悵。

translations.literal: Yet those who do not know your servant will surely think your servant bears the traces of rivalry—I follow this thought with lingering sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: Yet those who do not know me will surely think I bear the traces of rivalry—I follow this thought with lingering sorrow.

sentences.zh: 臣與炳之周旋，俱被恩接，不宜復生厚薄。

translations.literal: Your servant and Bingzhi have associated together; both received gracious treatment. One ought not again to give rise to favor or disfavor.
translations.idiomatic: Bingzhi and I have associated together; both of us received gracious treatment. One ought not again to give rise to favor or disfavor.

sentences.zh: 太尉昨與臣言，說炳之有諸不可，非唯一條，遠近相崇畏，震動四海，凡短人辦得致此，更復可嘉。

translations.literal: Yesterday the Grand Commander spoke with your servant, saying Bingzhi has many offenses, not only one item. Near and far regard him with reverence and fear; the realm is shaken. That a man of small stature could bring this about is again worthy of note.
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday the Grand Commander spoke with me, saying Bingzhi has many offenses, not only one item. Near and far regard him with reverence and fear, and the realm is shaken. That a man of small stature could bring this about is again worthy of note.

sentences.zh: 虞秀之門生事之，累味珍肴，未嘗有乏，其外別貢，豈可具詳。

translations.literal: A protege of Yu Xiuzhi waited on him; successive dishes of rare delicacies were never lacking. Other tributes besides these—how could they be fully detailed?
translations.idiomatic: A protege of Yu Xiuzhi waited on him; successive dishes of rare delicacies were never lacking. Other tributes besides these—how could they be fully detailed?

sentences.zh: 炳之門中不問大小，誅求張幼緒，幼緒轉無以堪命。

translations.literal: In Bingzhi's household, great and small without distinction extort from Zhang Youxu; Youxu in turn could not bear it.
translations.idiomatic: In Bingzhi's household, great and small without distinction extort from Zhang Youxu; Youxu in turn could not bear it.

sentences.zh: 炳之先與劉德願殊惡，德願自持琵琶甚精麗。

translations.literal: Bingzhi had first been on very bad terms with Liu Deyuan; Deyuan's own pipa was extremely fine and beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: Bingzhi had first been on very bad terms with Liu Deyuan; Deyuan's own pipa was extremely fine and beautiful.

sentences.zh: 遺之，便復款然。

translations.literal: When Bingzhi sent it to him as a gift, they became friendly again at once.
translations.idiomatic: When Bingzhi sent it to him as a gift, they became friendly again at once.

sentences.zh: 市令盛馥進數百口材助營宅，恐人知，作虛買券。

translations.literal: Market Magistrate Sheng Fu presented several hundred cartloads of timber to help build his residence; fearing people would know, he made a false purchase contract.
translations.idiomatic: Market Magistrate Sheng Fu presented several hundred cartloads of timber to help build his residence; fearing people would know, he made a false purchase contract.

sentences.zh: 劉道錫驟有所輸，傾南俸之半。

translations.literal: Liu Daoxi suddenly made some payment—half his southern salary gone.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Daoxi suddenly made some payment—half his southern salary gone.

sentences.zh: 劉雍自謂得其力助，事之如父，夏中送甘庶，若新發於州。

translations.literal: Liu Yong considered that he owed his strength and aid, and served him like a father. In midsummer he sent him sugarcane, as if freshly shipped from the province.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yong considered that he owed his strength and aid, and served him like a father. In midsummer he sent him sugarcane, as if freshly shipped from the province.

sentences.zh: 國吏運載樵荻，無輟於道。

translations.literal: State clerks transported firewood and reeds without pause on the roads.
translations.idiomatic: State clerks transported firewood and reeds without pause on the roads.

sentences.zh: 諸見人有物，鮮或不求。

translations.literal: When he saw anyone with goods, if they were fresh, he rarely did not demand them.
translations.idiomatic: When he saw anyone with goods, if they were fresh, he rarely did not demand them.

sentences.zh: 聞劉遵考有材；

translations.literal: Hearing that Liu Zunkao had timber;
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Liu Zunkao had timber;

sentences.zh: 便乞材，見好燭盤，便復乞之。

translations.literal: he asked for timber; seeing a fine candle stand, he again asked for it.
translations.idiomatic: he asked for timber; seeing a fine candle stand, he again asked for it.

sentences.zh: 選用不平，不可一二。

translations.literal: Unfairness in selection and appointment—more than one or two instances.
translations.idiomatic: Unfairness in selection and appointment—more than one or two instances.

sentences.zh: 太尉又云，炳之都無共事之體，凡所選舉，悉是其意，政令太尉知耳。

translations.literal: The Grand Commander also said that Bingzhi entirely lacked the bearing of one who serves jointly in office. All selections and promotions were entirely according to his will; the Grand Commander merely knew about them.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Commander also said that Bingzhi entirely lacked the bearing of one who serves jointly in office. All selections and promotions were entirely according to his will; the Grand Commander merely knew about them.

sentences.zh: 論虞秀之作黃門，太尉不正答和，故得停。

translations.literal: When Yu Xiuzhi's appointment as Yellow Gate Attendant was discussed, the Grand Commander did not immediately agree—and so it was halted.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Xiuzhi's appointment as Yellow Gate Attendant was discussed, the Grand Commander did not immediately agree—and so it was halted.

sentences.zh: 太尉近與炳之疏，欲用德原兒作州西曹，炳之乃啟用為主簿，即語德願，德願謝太尉。

translations.literal: Recently the Grand Commander grew distant from Bingzhi and wished to appoint Deyuan's son as Western Aide of the province. Bingzhi then memorialized to appoint him as Chief Clerk and immediately told Deyuan, who thanked the Grand Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Recently the Grand Commander grew distant from Bingzhi and wished to appoint Deyuan's son as Western Aide of the province. Bingzhi then memorialized to appoint him as Chief Clerk and immediately told Deyuan, who thanked the Grand Commander.

sentences.zh: 前後漏泄賣恩，亦復何極，縱不加罪，故宜出之。

translations.literal: Leaking secrets and selling favors before and after—again how limitless! Even if no additional crime is imposed, he ought for that reason alone to be sent out.
translations.idiomatic: Leaking secrets and selling favors before and after—again how limitless! Even if no additional crime is imposed, he ought for that reason alone to be sent out.

sentences.zh: 士庶忿疾之，非直項羽楚歌而已也。

translations.literal: Scholars and commoners hate and resent him—not merely the Chu songs around Xiang Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars and commoners hate and resent him—not merely the Chu songs around Xiang Yu.

sentences.zh: 自從裴、劉刑罰以來，諸將陳力百倍，今日事實好惡可問。

translations.literal: Since the punishments of Pei and Liu, the various generals have exerted themselves a hundredfold; today's facts, good and bad, can be asked about.
translations.idiomatic: Since the punishments of Pei and Liu, the various generals have exerted themselves a hundredfold; today's facts, good and bad, can be asked about.

sentences.zh: 若赫然發憤，顯明法憲，陛下便可閑臥紫闥，無復一事也。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty now rouses his wrath and clearly displays the laws, Your Majesty may then lie at ease in the purple inner chambers with never another matter to attend to!"
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty now rouses your wrath and clearly displays the laws, you may then lie at ease in the purple inner chambers with never another matter to attend to!"

sentences.zh: 太祖欲出炳之為丹陽，又以問尚之。

translations.literal: Taizu wished to send Bingzhi out as Administrator of Danyang and again questioned Shangzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu wished to send Bingzhi out as Administrator of Danyang and again questioned Shangzhi.

sentences.zh: 尚之答曰：「臣既乏賈生應對之才，又謝汲公犯顏之直，至於侍坐仰酬，每不能盡。

translations.literal: Shangzhi answered: "Your servant lacks Jia Yi's talent for responsive eloquence and Ji An's forthright courage in offending the monarch. As for sitting in attendance and answering face to face, I can never fully exhaust the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhi answered: "Your servant lacks Jia Yi's talent for responsive eloquence and Ji An's forthright courage in offending the monarch. As for sitting in attendance and answering face to face, I can never fully exhaust the matter.

sentences.zh: 昨出伏復深思，祇有愚滯，今之事蹟，異口同音，便是彰著，政未測得物之數耳。

translations.literal: Yesterday when I left I again bowed and deeply considered. I have only foolishness and slowness. Today's facts, same mouth same sound—are already clear and manifest. It is merely that one cannot yet measure how far things extend.
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday when I left I again bowed and deeply considered. I have only foolishness and slowness. Today's facts, same mouth same sound—are already clear and manifest. It is merely that one cannot yet measure how far things extend.

sentences.zh: 可為蹈罪負恩，無所復少。

translations.literal: One may say he treads on guilt and bears ingratitude—there is nothing left that is slight.
translations.idiomatic: One may say he treads on guilt and bears ingratitude—there is nothing left that is slight.

sentences.zh: 且居官失和，未有此比。

translations.literal: And in losing harmony in office, never has there been the like.
translations.idiomatic: And in losing harmony in office, never has there been the like.

sentences.zh: 陛下遲遲舊恩，未忍窮法，為弘之大，莫復過此。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, out of lingering old kindness, has not yet been able to exhaust the law. For the greatness of magnanimity, nothing surpasses this.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, out of lingering old kindness, has not yet been able to exhaust the law. For the greatness of magnanimity, nothing surpasses this.

sentences.zh: 方復有尹京赫赫之授，恐悉心奉國之人，於此而息；

translations.literal: Yet one would again grant him the glorious appointment of governing the capital—I fear those who give their whole hearts to serving the state will on this account cease;
translations.idiomatic: Yet one would again grant him the glorious appointment of governing the capital—I fear those who give their whole hearts to serving the state will on this account cease;

sentences.zh: 貪狼恣意者，歲月滋甚。

translations.literal: the greedy and savage who do as they please will from month to year grow worse.
translations.idiomatic: the greedy and savage who do as they please will from month to year grow worse.

sentences.zh: 非但虧點王化，乃治亂所由。

translations.literal: This not only mars the royal transformation—it is the source from which order and chaos arise.
translations.idiomatic: This not only mars the royal transformation—it is the source from which order and chaos arise.

sentences.zh: 如臣所聞天下論議，炳之常塵累日月，未見一豪增輝。

translations.literal: As your servant has heard, discussion throughout the realm holds that Bingzhi constantly dims and burdens the sun and moon; one has not seen a single hair's worth add luster.
translations.idiomatic: As I have heard, discussion throughout the realm holds that Bingzhi constantly dims and burdens the sun and moon; one has not seen a single hair's worth add luster.

sentences.zh: 今曲阿在水南，恩寵無異，而協首郡之榮，乃更成其形勢，便是老王雅也。

translations.literal: Now Qu'a is south of the river; favor and grace are no different. Yet the glory of a capital commandery would further expand his power—this would be the old case of Wang Ya.
translations.idiomatic: Now Qu'a is south of the river; favor and grace are no different. Yet the glory of a capital commandery would further expand his power—this would be the old case of Wang Ya.

sentences.zh: 古人云：『賞罰，雖堯、舜不能為治也。

translations.literal: The ancients said: 'Reward and punishment—even Yao and Shun cannot govern by that alone.'
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said: 'Reward and punishment—even Yao and Shun cannot govern by that alone.'

sentences.zh: 』陛下豈可坐損皇家之重，迷一凡人。

translations.literal: How can Your Majesty sit and diminish the weight of the imperial house, bewildered by one ordinary man?
translations.idiomatic: How can Your Majesty sit and diminish the weight of the imperial house, bewildered by one ordinary man?

sentences.zh: 事若復在可否之間，亦不敢苟陳穴管。

translations.literal: If the matter were again between yes and no, your servant would not dare casually offer a narrow view from a hole.
translations.idiomatic: If the matter were again between yes and no, I would not dare casually offer a narrow view from a hole.

sentences.zh: 今之枉直，明白灼然，而叡王令王，反更不悟，令賈誼、劉向重生，豈不慷慨流涕於聖世邪！

translations.literal: Today right and wrong are clear as fire, yet the sage king who makes kings is all the more uncomprehending. If Jia Yi and Liu Xiang were reborn, would they not weep in indignation in this sacred age!
translations.idiomatic: Today right and wrong are clear as fire, yet the sage king who makes kings is all the more uncomprehending. If Jia Yi and Liu Xiang were reborn, would they not weep in indignation in this sacred age!

sentences.zh: 臣昔啟范曄，當時亦懼犯觸之尤，苟是愚懷所挹，政自不能不舒達，所謂雖九死而不悔者也。

translations.literal: Your servant formerly memorialized on Fan Ye. At the time I likewise feared the offense of having touched and offended. If it was what my foolish heart drew up, I truly could not but express it openly—what they call 'though nine deaths, still no regret.'
translations.idiomatic: I formerly memorialized on Fan Ye. At the time I likewise feared the offense of having touched and offended. If it was what my foolish heart drew up, I truly could not but express it openly—what they call 'though nine deaths, still no regret.'

sentences.zh: 謂炳之且外出，若能脩改，在職著稱，還亦不難，則可得少明國典，粗酬四海之誚。

translations.literal: One may say that once Bingzhi goes out, if he can reform, perform well in office and win renown, reinstatement would not be difficult. Then one could at least slightly clarify the statutes of the state and roughly answer the reproaches of the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: One may say that once Bingzhi goes out, if he can reform, perform well in office and win renown, reinstatement would not be difficult. Then one could at least slightly clarify the statutes of the state and roughly answer the reproaches of the four seas.

sentences.zh: 今愆釁如山，榮任不損，炳之若復有彰大之罪，誰復敢以聞述。

translations.literal: Now faults and offenses are like mountains, yet glory and office are undiminished. If Bingzhi again commits greater glaring crimes, who will again dare report them?
translations.idiomatic: Now faults and offenses are like mountains, yet glory and office are undiminished. If Bingzhi again commits greater glaring crimes, who will again dare report them?

sentences.zh: 且自非殊勳異績，亦何足塞今日之尤。

translations.literal: Moreover, unless there were extraordinary merit and unusual achievement, what would suffice to fill today's blame?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, unless there were extraordinary merit and unusual achievement, what would suffice to fill today's blame?

sentences.zh: 歷觀古今，未有眾過藉藉，受貨數百萬，更得高官厚祿如今者也。

translations.literal: Reviewing past and present, never has one seen a man of numerous notorious offenses who accepted bribes of millions and yet again received high office and rich emolument as now.
translations.idiomatic: Reviewing past and present, never has one seen a man of numerous notorious offenses who accepted bribes of millions and yet again received high office and rich emolument as now.

sentences.zh: 臣每念聖化中有此事，未嘗不痛心疾首。

translations.literal: Each time your servant thinks that in the sacred transformation there is this matter, I have never failed to grieve to the heart and ache in the head.
translations.idiomatic: Each time I think that in the sacred transformation there is this matter, I have never failed to grieve to the heart and ache in the head.

sentences.zh: 設令臣等數人縱橫狼藉復如此，不審當復云何處之。

translations.literal: Suppose your servant and several others wantonly spread chaos again like this—I know not how Your Majesty would dispose of us.
translations.idiomatic: Suppose I and several others wantonly spread chaos again like this—I know not how Your Majesty would dispose of us.

sentences.zh: 近啟賈充遠鎮，今亦何足分，外出恐是策之良者。

translations.literal: Recently I memorialized that Jia Chong should be sent far to a garrison. Today too he shares nothing of Bingzhi's blame. Sending him out would probably be a sound stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Recently I memorialized that Jia Chong should be sent far to a garrison. Today too he shares nothing of Bingzhi's blame. Sending him out would probably be a sound stratagem.

sentences.zh: 臣知陛下不能采臣言，故是臣不能盡己之愚至耳。

translations.literal: Your servant knows Your Majesty cannot adopt your servant's words—thus it is merely that your servant cannot exhaust his own foolishness to the end.
translations.idiomatic: I know Your Majesty cannot adopt my words—thus it is merely that I cannot exhaust my own foolishness to the end.

sentences.zh: 今蒙恩榮者不少，臣何為獨懇懇於斯，實是尊主樂治之意。

translations.literal: Now those who receive grace and glory are not few. Why should your servant alone speak earnestly in this? It is truly the intent to honor the sovereign and rejoice in good governance.
translations.idiomatic: Now those who receive grace and glory are not few. Why should I alone speak earnestly in this? It is truly the intent to honor the sovereign and rejoice in good governance.

sentences.zh: 伏願試更垂察」

translations.literal: I humbly pray you try again to look down and examine."
translations.idiomatic: I humbly pray you try again to look down and examine."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「臣見劉伯寵大慷慨炳之所行，云有人送張幼緒，幼緒語人，吾雖得一縣，負三十萬錢，庾沖遠乃當送至新林，見縛束，猶未得解手。

translations.literal: He also said: "Your servant saw Liu Bochong become greatly indignant at Bingzhi's conduct. He said someone sent for Zhang Youxu; Youxu told people: 'Though I gain one county, I owe three hundred thousand cash.' Yu Chongyuan was about to send him to Xinlin—when he saw the bundles he still could not free his hands."
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "I saw Liu Bochong become greatly indignant at Bingzhi's conduct. He said someone sent for Zhang Youxu; Youxu told people: 'Though I gain one county, I owe three hundred thousand cash.' Yu Chongyuan was about to send him to Xinlin—when he saw the bundles he still could not free his hands."

sentences.zh: 荀萬秋嘗詣炳之，值一客姓夏侯，主人問『有好牛不？

translations.literal: Xun Wanqiu once called on Bingzhi when there was a guest surnamed Xiahou. The host asked, 'Have you a good ox?'
translations.idiomatic: Xun Wanqiu once called on Bingzhi when there was a guest surnamed Xiahou. The host asked, 'Have you a good ox?'

translations.literal: He said: 'None.'
translations.idiomatic: He said: 'None.'

sentences.zh: 』問『有好馬不？

translations.literal: He asked, 'Have you a good horse?'
translations.idiomatic: He asked, 'Have you a good horse?'

sentences.zh: 』又云：『無。

translations.literal: Again he said: 'None.'
translations.idiomatic: Again he said: 'None.'

sentences.zh: 政有佳驢耳。

translations.literal: I have only a fine donkey.'
translations.idiomatic: I have only a fine donkey.'

sentences.zh: 』炳之便答：『甚是所欲。

translations.literal: Bingzhi at once answered: 'That is exactly what I desire.'
translations.idiomatic: Bingzhi at once answered: 'That is exactly what I desire.'

sentences.zh: 』客出門，遂與相聞索之。

translations.literal: When the guest left the door, Bingzhi immediately sent word to ask for it.
translations.idiomatic: When the guest left the door, Bingzhi immediately sent word to ask for it.

sentences.zh: 劉道錫云是炳之所舉，就道錫索嫁女具及祠器，乃當百萬數。

translations.literal: Liu Daoxi said it was Bingzhi who had recommended him; Bingzhi then asked Daoxi for bridal outfit and ritual vessels—worth perhaps a million in all.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Daoxi said it was Bingzhi who had recommended him; Bingzhi then asked Daoxi for bridal outfit and ritual vessels—worth perhaps a million in all.

sentences.zh: 猶謂不然。

translations.literal: One still thinks it cannot be so.
translations.idiomatic: One still thinks it cannot be so.

sentences.zh: 選令史章龍向臣說，亦歎其受納之過，言『實得嫁女具，銅爐四人舉乃勝，細葛斗帳等物，不可稱數。

translations.literal: Selection Clerk Zhang Long told your servant, also sighing over his acceptance of bribes. He said, 'He really received the bridal outfit—a bronze brazier that four men could barely lift—and fine hemp gauze canopy covers and such things, beyond count.'
translations.idiomatic: Selection Clerk Zhang Long told me, also sighing over his acceptance of bribes. He said, 'He really received the bridal outfit—a bronze brazier that four men could barely lift—and fine hemp gauze canopy covers and such things, beyond count.'

sentences.zh: '在尚書中，令奴酤酃酒，利其百十，亦是立臺閣所無，不審少簡聖聽不？

translations.literal: In the Ministry of Personnel, he had a slave sell Luling wine and profit one or two hundred—this too is unheard of in the establishment of the upper offices. I know not whether Your Majesty's sacred hearing might briefly examine it?
translations.idiomatic: In the Ministry of Personnel, he had a slave sell Luling wine and profit one or two hundred—this too is unheard of in the establishment of the upper offices. I know not whether Your Majesty's sacred hearing might briefly examine it?

sentences.zh: 恐仰傷日月之明，臣竊為之歎息。」

translations.literal: I fear it will wound the brightness of the sun and moon above. Your servant privately sighs for this."
translations.idiomatic: I fear it will wound the brightness of the sun and moon above. I privately sigh for this."

sentences.zh: 太祖乃可有司之奏，免炳之官。

translations.literal: Taizu then approved the memorial of the relevant officials and dismissed Bingzhi from office.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu then approved the memorial of the relevant officials and dismissed Bingzhi from office.

sentences.zh: 是歲，元嘉二十五年也。

translations.literal: This year was the twenty-fifth year of Yuanjia.
translations.idiomatic: That was the twenty-fifth year of Yuanjia.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，卒於家，時年六十三。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he died at home, aged sixty-three at the time.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year he died at home, at the age of sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 太祖錄其宿誠，追復本官。

translations.literal: Taizu recorded his longtime loyalty and posthumously restored him to his original office.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu took note of his long-standing loyalty and posthumously restored him to his former office.

sentences.zh: 二子季遠、弘遠。

translations.literal: Two sons: Jiyuan and Hongyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Jiyuan and Hongyuan.

sentences.zh: 謝方明

translations.literal: Xie Fangming
translations.idiomatic: Xie Fangming

sentences.zh: 謝方明，陳郡陽夏人，尚書僕射景仁從祖弟也。

translations.literal: Xie Fangming was a native of Yangxia in Chen commandery, a first cousin once removed of the Masters of Writing and Right Deputy Minister Jingren.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Fangming came from Yangxia in Chen commandery and was a first cousin once removed of Jingren, Deputy Minister of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 祖鐵，永嘉太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Tie was Administrator of Yongjia.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Tie had served as Administrator of Yongjia.

sentences.zh: 父沖，中書侍郎。

translations.literal: His father Chong was Attendant of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chong had been Attendant of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 家在會稽，謝病歸，除黃門侍郎，不就。

translations.literal: His family was in Kuaiji; citing illness he returned home. He was appointed Yellow Gate Attendant but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: His family lived in Kuaiji. He returned home on grounds of illness, was appointed Yellow Gate Attendant, and declined the post.

sentences.zh: 為孫恩所殺，追贈散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was killed by Sun En and was posthumously enfeoffed as Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Sun En killed him, and he was posthumously awarded the title Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 方明隨伯父吳興太守邈在郡，孫恩寇會稽，東土諸郡皆回應，吳興民胡桀、郜驃破東遷縣，方明勸邈避之，不從，賊至被害，方明逃竄遂免。

translations.literal: Fangming followed his paternal uncle, Administrator of Wuxing Miao, in the commandery. Sun En raided Kuaiji, and all the eastern commanderies responded in turn. The Wuxing commoners Hu Jie and Gao Biao overran Dongqian county. Fangming urged Miao to flee; Miao would not listen. When the bandits arrived, Miao was killed; Fangming fled and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Fangming was with his uncle Miao, who served as Administrator of Wuxing. When Sun En attacked Kuaiji and commanderies throughout the east answered his call, the Wuxing commoners Hu Jie and Gao Biao stormed Dongqian county. Fangming urged Miao to withdraw, but Miao refused. The rebels arrived and killed Miao; Fangming fled and survived.

sentences.zh: 初，邈舅子長樂馮嗣之及北方學士馮翊仇玄達，俱往吳興投邈，並舍之郡學，禮待甚簡。

translations.literal: Initially, Miao's nephew by marriage Feng Sizhi of Changle and the northern scholar Qiu Xuanda of Fufeng both went to Wuxing to seek refuge with Miao. Both were lodged in the commandery school, and the courtesy extended them was very sparing.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Miao's nephew by marriage Feng Sizhi of Changle and the northern scholar Qiu Xuanda of Fufeng had both gone to Wuxing to place themselves under Miao's protection. Both were housed at the commandery school, but received only the barest courtesy.

sentences.zh: 二人並忿慍，遂與恩通謀。

translations.literal: Both men were alike resentful and angry, and thereupon conspired with En.
translations.idiomatic: Resentful and indignant, the two men soon entered into conspiracy with Sun En.

sentences.zh: 恩嘗為嗣之等從者，夜入郡，見邈眾，遁，不悟。

translations.literal: En once came as a follower of Sizhi and the others. Entering the commandery at night, he saw Miao's crowd and fled without being recognized.
translations.idiomatic: Sun En once came as a follower of Sizhi and the others. Entering the commandery seat by night, he saw Miao surrounded by his retainers and slipped away unrecognized.

sentences.zh: 本欲於吳興起兵，事趣不果，乃遷於會稽。

translations.literal: He had originally intended to raise troops in Wuxing, but the affair's course did not succeed, so he moved to Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: He had originally planned to raise arms in Wuxing, but the attempt failed, and he shifted operations to Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 及郜等攻郡，嗣之、玄達並豫其謀。

translations.literal: When Gao and the others attacked the commandery, Sizhi and Xuanda both took part in their plot.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao and the others assaulted the commandery, both Sizhi and Xuanda were involved in the conspiracy.

sentences.zh: 劉牢之、謝琰等討恩，恩走入海，嗣之等不得同去，方更聚合。

translations.literal: Liu Laozhi, Xie Yan, and others campaigned against En. En fled into the sea. Sizhi and the others could not go with him and had just begun to regroup.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Laozhi, Xie Yan, and others marched against Sun En, who fled out to sea. Unable to follow him, Sizhi and his cohort were only then regrouping.

sentences.zh: 方明結邈門生義故得百餘人，掩討嗣之等，悉禽而手刃之。

translations.literal: Fangming gathered more than a hundred of Miao's former students and old associates, launched a surprise attack on Sizhi and the others, captured them all, and personally ran them through with the blade.
translations.idiomatic: Fangming rallied more than a hundred of Miao's former students and old associates, launched a surprise strike against Sizhi and the others, captured them all, and personally executed them with his own blade.

sentences.zh: 于時荒亂之後，吉凶禮廢。

translations.literal: At that time, after the wild disorder, rites of fortune and misfortune had fallen into disuse.
translations.idiomatic: In that age of ruin and chaos, the rites governing life and death had fallen into neglect.

sentences.zh: 方明合門遇禍，資產無遺，而營舉凶事，盡其力用；

translations.literal: Fangming's entire household had met calamity, and no assets remained; yet he undertook the mourning arrangements and exhausted every resource at his command;
translations.idiomatic: Fangming's whole household had been struck by disaster, and nothing of their property survived; yet he still managed the funeral rites and spent everything he could muster;

sentences.zh: 數月之間，葬送並畢，平世備禮，無以加也。

translations.literal: Within the space of several months, burial and sending-off were all complete; the full rites of peaceful times could not have surpassed this.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few months he had seen to burial and obsequies completely—such ceremony as might have been expected even in peaceful times could hardly have exceeded it.

sentences.zh: 頃之，孫恩重沒會稽，謝琰見害。

translations.literal: Before long, Sun En again overran Kuaiji, and Xie Yan was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Sun En overran Kuaiji again, and Xie Yan was killed.

sentences.zh: 恩購求方明甚急。

translations.literal: En offered a reward for Fangming with great urgency.
translations.idiomatic: Sun En urgently offered a rich reward for Fangming's capture.

sentences.zh: 方明於上虞載母妹奔東陽，由黃蘖嶠出鄱陽，附載還都，寄居國子學。

translations.literal: Fangming at Shangyu loaded his mother and younger sister and fled toward Dongyang, passed through Huangbo Ridge into Poyang, took passage on a returning boat to the capital, and lodged in the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: At Shangyu, Fangming took his mother and younger sister and fled toward Dongyang, crossing Huangbo Ridge into Poyang, then boarding a returning vessel to the capital and lodging at the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 流離險厄，屯苦備經，而貞立之操，在約無改。

translations.literal: Exile, peril, hardship, and every affliction he passed through—yet his steadfast integrity, even in want, never changed.
translations.idiomatic: He endured exile, danger, and every hardship of privation, yet his steadfast character never wavered even in straitened circumstances.

sentences.zh: 元興元年，桓玄克京邑，丹陽尹卞範之勢傾朝野，欲以女嫁方明，使尚書吏部郎王騰譬說備至，方明終不回。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanxing, Huan Xuan seized the capital. Chief Administrator of Danyang Bian Fanzhi's power tilted the court and countryside. Wishing to marry his daughter to Fangming, he sent Masters of Writing Personnel Section Director Wang Teng to persuade him with utmost eloquence, but Fangming in the end would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanxing, Huan Xuan seized the capital. Bian Fanzhi, Chief Administrator of Danyang, wielded power that dominated court and countryside alike. He wished to give his daughter to Fangming in marriage and sent Wang Teng, Director of the Personnel Section in the Masters of Writing, to persuade him with every argument at his disposal—but Fangming would not be moved.

sentences.zh: 桓玄聞而賞之，即除著作佐郎，補司徒王謐主簿。

translations.literal: Huan Xuan heard of this and admired him, immediately appointing him Assistant Editorial Director and supplementing him as Chief Clerk to Grand Preceptor Wang Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan heard of this and admired him, immediately appointing him Assistant Editorial Director and then assigning him as Chief Clerk to Grand Preceptor Wang Mi.

sentences.zh: 從兄景仁舉為高祖中兵主簿。

translations.literal: His first cousin Jingren recommended him as Central Army Chief Clerk under Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Jingren recommended him to Gaozu for the post of Central Army Chief Clerk.

sentences.zh: 方明事思忠益，知無不為。

translations.literal: In service Fangming thought only of loyalty and benefit; where there was knowledge, there was nothing he would not do.
translations.idiomatic: In his service Fangming devoted himself to loyal counsel and gave his all; where he saw a need, he did whatever he could.

sentences.zh: 高祖謂之曰：「愧未有瓜衍之賞，且當與卿共豫章國祿。

translations.literal: Gaozu said to him: "I am ashamed not to have a Guayan-style reward; for the time being let us share the salary of the State of Yuzhang together.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu told him, "I regret that I have no Guayan-scale reward to offer you—for now, let us share the income of the State of Yuzhang between us.

sentences.zh: 」屢加賞賜。

translations.literal: Rewards and gifts were repeatedly added.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu showered him with rewards again and again.

sentences.zh: 方明嚴恪，善自居遇，雖處暗室，未嘗有惰容。

translations.literal: Fangming was stern and strict, good at comporting himself; even in a dark room he never showed a lazy bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Fangming was strict and disciplined, careful in his conduct; even alone in a dark room he never showed a negligent air.

sentences.zh: 無他伎能，自然有雅韻。

translations.literal: He had no other skills, yet naturally possessed elegant bearing.
translations.idiomatic: He possessed no special talents, yet had a natural grace and refinement.

sentences.zh: 從兄混有重名，唯歲節朝宗而已。

translations.literal: His cousin Hun had a weighty reputation; they met only at New Year festivals for clan observance.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Hun was widely celebrated, yet the two met only at New Year's clan gatherings.

sentences.zh: 丹陽尹劉穆之權重當時，朝野輻輳，不與穆之相識者，唯有混、方明、郗僧施、蔡廓四人而已；

translations.literal: Chief Administrator of Danyang Liu Muzhi's authority weighed on the age; court and countryside converged on him like wheel spokes. Those in court who did not know Muzhi numbered only Hun, Fangming, Chi Sengshi, and Cai Kuo among them;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Muzhi, Chief Administrator of Danyang, held power that dominated the age, and court and countryside alike thronged about him. Of those in official life who did not know Muzhi personally, there were only Hun, Fangming, Chi Sengshi, and Cai Kuo;

sentences.zh: 穆之甚以為恨。

translations.literal: Muzhi deeply resented this.
translations.idiomatic: Muzhi deeply resented this.

sentences.zh: 方明、廓後往造之，大悅，白高祖曰：「謝方明可謂名家駒。

translations.literal: Fangming and Kuo later went to call on him; he was greatly pleased and reported to Gaozu: "Xie Fangming may be called a colt of a great house.
translations.idiomatic: When Fangming and Kuo later visited him, Muzhi was delighted and told Gaozu, "Xie Fangming is a true thoroughbred of a great clan.

sentences.zh: 直置便自是臺鼎人，無論復有才用。

translations.literal: Simply set in place, he would at once be a man for the highest offices, to say nothing of further talent and ability.
translations.idiomatic: Even without further cultivation he would be a man destined for the highest offices, quite apart from whatever talent and ability he may possess.

sentences.zh: 」頃之，轉從事中郎，仍為左將軍道憐長史、高祖命府內眾事，皆咨決之。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Attendant-in-Ordinary, then became Chief of Staff to General of the Left Daolin, and Gaozu charged that all matters within the commandery seat should be referred to him for decision.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to Attendant-in-Ordinary, then served as Chief of Staff to General of the Left Daolin, with Gaozu directing that all matters within the commandery seat be resolved on his counsel.

sentences.zh: 隨府轉中軍長史。

translations.literal: Following the commandery seat he transferred to Chief of Staff of the Central Army.
translations.idiomatic: When the commandery seat moved, he became Chief of Staff of the Central Army.

sentences.zh: 尋更加晉陵太守，復為驃騎長史、南郡相，委任如初。

translations.literal: Before long he was additionally appointed Administrator of Jinling; again he served as Chief of Staff under the Cavalry General and Chancellor of Nan commandery, entrusted as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon given the additional post of Administrator of Jinling, then again served as Chief of Staff to the Cavalry General while also governing Nan commandery, with trust as unwavering as before.

sentences.zh: 嘗年終，江陵縣獄囚事無輕重，悉散聽歸家，使過正三日還到。

translations.literal: On one New Year's Eve, the prisoners of Jiangling county—regardless of the severity of their offenses—were all released and allowed to return home, ordered to come back after the third day of the New Year.
translations.idiomatic: At one year's end, he had every prisoner in Jiangling county, regardless of offense, released to go home on the condition that they return after the third day of the New Year.

sentences.zh: 罪應入重者有二十餘人，綱紀以下，莫不疑懼。

translations.literal: Those whose crimes deserved heavy punishment numbered more than twenty. From the chief clerks down, none did not doubt and fear.
translations.idiomatic: More than twenty faced penalties that could carry heavy punishment; from the staff officers down, everyone was baffled and alarmed.

sentences.zh: 時晉陵郡送故主簿弘季盛、徐壽之並隨在西，固諫以為：「昔人雖有其事，或是記籍過言。

translations.literal: At that time the Jinling commandery sent its former Chief Clerks Hong Jisheng and Xu Shouzhi, both accompanying them in the west, who firmly remonstrated saying: "People of old indeed had such a practice, but perhaps that was an excess of the records.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, two former chief clerks sent from Jinling commandery, Hong Jisheng and Xu Shouzhi, who were serving with him in the west, strongly objected: "Earlier ages may indeed have done such things, but perhaps those accounts overstate the case.

sentences.zh: 且當今民情偽薄，不可以古義相許。

translations.literal: And the temperament of the people today is false and shallow; one cannot hold them to the meaning of antiquity."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the temper of the people today is deceitful and shallow; one cannot expect them to live up to the standards of antiquity."

sentences.zh: 」方明不納，一時遣之。

translations.literal: Fangming would not accept this and at once sent them all off.
translations.idiomatic: Fangming ignored them and released the prisoners at once.

sentences.zh: 囚及父兄皆驚喜涕泣，以為就死無恨。

translations.literal: The prisoners and their fathers and elder brothers all were astonished, delighted, and wept, thinking that even to go to death would be without regret.
translations.idiomatic: The prisoners and their fathers and elder brothers wept for joy, saying they could face death without regret.

sentences.zh: 至期，有重罪二人不還，方明不聽討捕。

translations.literal: When the deadline came, two men guilty of heavy crimes did not return. Fangming would not listen to pursuit and capture.
translations.idiomatic: When the deadline came, two of the serious offenders failed to return—but Fangming refused to send anyone after them.

sentences.zh: 其一人醉不能歸，逮二日乃反；

translations.literal: One man, drunk, could not return; only after two days did he come back;
translations.idiomatic: One had been too drunk to return and showed up two days late;

sentences.zh: 餘一囚十日不至，五官硃千期請見欲白討之，方明知為囚事，使左右謝五官不須入，囚自當反。

translations.literal: The remaining prisoner did not arrive for ten days. The Five Offices official Zhu Qianqi requested an audience, intending to report and seek pursuit. Fangming knew it concerned the prisoner affair and had his attendants tell the Five Offices official that he need not enter—the prisoner would return on his own.
translations.idiomatic: The other did not appear for ten days. Zhu Qianqi of the Five Offices asked for an audience to report the lapse and request a hunt, but Fangming, knowing it concerned the prisoners, had an attendant tell Zhu that he need not come in—the man would return of his own accord.

sentences.zh: 囚逡巡墟裏，不能自歸，鄉村責讓之，率領將送，遂竟無逃亡者。

translations.literal: The prisoner wandered the hamlets and lanes and could not bring himself to return. The village folk rebuked him and led and escorted him back, and in the end there were none who fled.
translations.idiomatic: That prisoner wandered the lanes of his neighborhood, unable to bring himself home, until the villagers rebuked him and led him back under escort—and in the end not a single man absconded.

sentences.zh: 遠近咸嘆服焉。

translations.literal: Near and far all sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Near and far alike marvelled at his judgment.

sentences.zh: 遭母憂，去職。

translations.literal: He encountered mourning for his mother and left office.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, he left office to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 服闋，為宋臺尚書吏部郎。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he served as Personnel Director in the Masters of Writing of the Song Platform.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he served as Personnel Director in the Masters of Writing of the Song Platform.

sentences.zh: 高祖受命，遷侍中。

translations.literal: When Gaozu received the Mandate, he was transferred to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, he was promoted to Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 永初三年，出為丹陽尹，有能名。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongchu he went out as Chief Administrator of Danyang, with a reputation for competence.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongchu he was appointed Chief Administrator of Danyang and earned a name for capable administration.

sentences.zh: 轉會稽太守。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Administrator of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Administrator of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 江東民戶殷盛，風俗峻刻，強弱相陵，奸吏蜂起，符書一下，文攝相續。

translations.literal: The households of the Jiangdong region were numerous and prosperous, the customs harsh and exacting; strong bullied weak, corrupt clerks swarmed like bees, and when an official dispatch arrived, documents of exaction followed one after another.
translations.idiomatic: East of the river the population was dense and prosperous, yet customs were harsh and unyielding: the strong preyed upon the weak, corrupt officials swarmed like bees, and whenever an official dispatch arrived a flood of coercive paperwork followed.

sentences.zh: 又罪及比伍，動相連坐，一人犯吏，則一村廢業，邑裏驚擾，狗吠達旦。

translations.literal: Further, guilt extended to neighbors in grouped households; at every turn there was collective punishment. When one man offended an official, then a whole village abandoned its livelihood; the hamlets were alarmed and disturbed, and dogs barked until dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Punishment extended by mutual responsibility to whole neighborhoods, so that the arrest of one man could idle an entire village; towns were in constant uproar and dogs barked until dawn.

sentences.zh: 方明深達治體，不拘文法，闊略苛細，務存綱領。

translations.literal: Fangming deeply understood the substance of governance; he did not bind himself to written law, broadly set aside petty strictness, and strove to preserve the essential framework.
translations.idiomatic: Fangming had a deep grasp of how governance actually worked; he did not bind himself slavishly to the code, set aside petty strictures, and kept his eye on essentials.

sentences.zh: 州臺符攝，即時宣下，緩民期會，展其辦舉；

translations.literal: When provincial and platform orders arrived, he at once proclaimed and sent them down, easing popular deadlines and extending time for completion;
translations.idiomatic: When orders came from the province or the central government he promulgated them promptly, but eased deadlines for the people and allowed more time for compliance;

sentences.zh: 郡縣監司，不得妄出，貴族豪士，莫敢犯禁，除比伍之坐，判久系之獄。

translations.literal: county and commandery overseers were not allowed to go out rashly; nobles and powerful men did not dare violate prohibitions; collective household punishments were abolished, and long-held imprisonments were adjudicated.
translations.idiomatic: he kept district and county inspectors from meddling at will, barred the wealthy elite from defying the law, abolished collective punishments, and cleared long-pending cases from the jails.

sentences.zh: 前後征伐，每兵運不充，悉發倩士庶；

translations.literal: In campaigns before and after, whenever military transport fell short, he fully conscripted hired labor from gentry and commoners;
translations.idiomatic: In successive campaigns, when military transport fell short he levied labor from gentry and commoners alike;

sentences.zh: 事既寧息，皆使還本。

translations.literal: when affairs had settled, all were sent back to their homes.
translations.idiomatic: but once the emergency passed he sent every one of them home.

sentences.zh: 而屬所刻害，或即以補吏。

translations.literal: Yet where subordinates had pressed unjust harm, some were at once appointed to fill clerk posts.
translations.idiomatic: Yet subordinates who had oppressed the people were sometimes rewarded with official posts.

sentences.zh: 守宰不明，與奪乖舛，人事不至，必被抑塞。

translations.literal: If administrators were unclear and grants and denials were perverse, when complaints did not reach the proper level, they were sure to be blocked and suppressed.
translations.idiomatic: When magistrates were incompetent or decisions capricious, grievances that never reached the top were invariably stifled.

sentences.zh: 方明簡汰精當，各慎所宜，雖服役十載，亦一朝從理，東土至今稱詠之。

translations.literal: Fangming sifted and selected with precision and fitness; each was placed where caution required. Even those who had served ten years were in one morning brought to justice; to this day the eastern region sings his praise.
translations.idiomatic: Fangming reviewed cases with precision and placed each man where he belonged; even those who had been forced into service for ten years were released in a single day. To this day the eastern region praises him in song.

sentences.zh: 性尤愛惜，未嘗有所是非，承代前人，不易其政。

translations.literal: By nature he was especially sparing; he never made judgments of right and wrong, succeeding earlier men without changing their policies.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially cautious by nature, rarely pronouncing judgments of right and wrong; when he succeeded a predecessor he left his policies unchanged.

sentences.zh: 有必宜改者，則以漸移變，使無跡可尋。

translations.literal: Where change was truly necessary, he altered things by gradual shifts so that no trace could be found.
translations.idiomatic: When change was truly needed, he altered things by degrees so that no one could tell precisely when or how the shift had been made.

sentences.zh: 元嘉三年，卒官，年四十七。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanjia he died in office, aged forty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yuanjia he died in office, at the age of forty-seven.

sentences.zh: 子惠連，幼而聰敏，年十歲，能屬文，族兄靈運深相知賞，事在《靈運傳》。

translations.literal: His son Huilian was clever and quick from youth. At ten he could compose linked prose; his clansman Lingyun deeply knew and admired him—the matter is in the Biography of Lingyun.
translations.idiomatic: His son Huilian was clever from childhood. At ten he could write polished prose; his kinsman Lingyun held him in high esteem—the account is in Lingyun's biography.

sentences.zh: 本州辟主簿，不就。

translations.literal: The province summoned him as Chief Clerk; he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The province offered him the post of chief clerk; he declined.

sentences.zh: 惠連先愛會稽郡吏杜德靈，及居父憂，贈以五言詩十餘首，文行於世。

translations.literal: Huilian had earlier loved Du Deling, a clerk of Kuaiji commandery. When he was in mourning for his father, he gave him more than ten pentasyllabic poems, and the writing circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Huilian had previously been enamored of Du Deling, a clerk in Kuaiji commandery; while in mourning for his father he sent him more than a dozen pentasyllabic poems, and the verses soon circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 坐被徙廢塞，不豫榮伍。

translations.literal: On account of this he was sentenced to banishment and confinement in the frontier, and was excluded from the ranks of honor.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was banished to the frontier and barred from official advancement.

sentences.zh: 尚書僕射殷景仁愛其才，因言次白太祖：「臣小兒時，便見世中有此文，而論者雲是謝惠連，其實非也。

translations.literal: Deputy Minister of the Masters of Writing Yin Jingren loved his talent and, on another matter, reported to Taizu: "When your servant was a small child, I already saw such writing in the world, and those who discussed it said it was Xie Huilian's—but it is not in fact so.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Jingren, Deputy Minister of the Masters of Writing, admired his talent and took occasion to tell Taizu, "When I was a child I already saw such writing in circulation, and some claimed it was Xie Huilian's—but it was not.

sentences.zh: 」太祖曰：「若如此，便應通之。

translations.literal: Taizu said: "If it is so, he ought to be reinstated.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu said, "If that is so, then he should be restored.

sentences.zh: 」元嘉七年，方為司徒彭城王義康法曹參軍。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yuanjia he was finally made Administrative Officer of the Law Section on the staff of Grand Preceptor Pengcheng Prince Yikang.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Yuanjia he was at last appointed Administrative Officer of the Law Section on the staff of Prince Yikang of Pengcheng as Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 是時義康治東府城，城塹中得古塚，為之改葬，使惠連為祭文，留信待成，其文甚美。

translations.literal: At that time Yikang was repairing the eastern headquarters city wall; an ancient tomb was found in the moat. They gave it a new burial and had Huilian compose the sacrificial text, keeping a messenger waiting until it was finished—the text was very fine.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Yikang was repairing the eastern headquarters wall when an ancient tomb was found in the moat. Yikang ordered a proper reburial and commissioned Huilian to write the funerary text, keeping a messenger waiting until the piece was finished—and the writing was superb.

sentences.zh: 又為《雪賦》，亦以高麗見奇。

translations.literal: He also wrote "Rhapsody on Snow," which likewise was admired for its lofty beauty.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote the "Rhapsody on Snow," which likewise astonished readers with its elegance.

sentences.zh: 文章並傳於世。

translations.literal: His literary works both passed down in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His writings remain in circulation to this day.

sentences.zh: 十年，卒，時年二十七。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he died, aged twenty-seven at the time.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he died, at the age of twenty-seven.

sentences.zh: 既早亡，且輕薄多尤累，故官位不顯。

translations.literal: Since he died early and moreover was frivolous with many faults and entanglements, his official rank was not illustrious.
translations.idiomatic: He died young, and his frivolity and many failings kept him from distinction in office.

sentences.zh: 無子。

translations.literal: He had no sons.
translations.idiomatic: He left no sons.

sentences.zh: 弟惠宣，竟陵王誕司徒從事中郎，臨川內史。

translations.literal: His younger brother Huixuan served as Attendant-in-Ordinary on the Grand Preceptor staff of Prince Dan of Jingling and as Administrator of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Huixuan served as Attendant-in-Ordinary on the Grand Preceptor staff of Prince Dan of Jingling and as Administrator of Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 江夷，字茂遠，濟陽考城人也。

translations.literal: Jiang Yi, courtesy name Maoyuan, was a native of Kaocheng in Jiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Yi, styled Maoyuan, came from Kaocheng in Jiyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖霖彡，晉護軍將軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Bin was Jin Protector-General of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Bin had served as Protector-General of the Army under Jin.

sentences.zh: 父敳，驃騎諮議參軍。

translations.literal: His father Ao was Advisory Staff Member under the Cavalry General.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ao had been an advisory officer on the staff of the Cavalry General.

sentences.zh: 夷少自藻厲，為後進之美。

translations.literal: Yi from youth cultivated and disciplined himself and was praised among the newer generation.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Yi refined himself with strict discipline and stood out among his generation.

sentences.zh: 州辟主簿，不就。

translations.literal: The province summoned him as Chief Clerk; he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The province offered him the post of chief clerk; he declined.

sentences.zh: 桓玄篡位，以為豫章王文學。

translations.literal: When Huan Xuan usurped the throne, Yi was made Literary Instructor to the Prince of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Xuan seized the throne, Yi was appointed Literary Instructor to the Prince of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 義旗建，高祖板為鎮軍行參軍，尋參大司馬琅邪王軍事，轉以公事免。

translations.literal: When the Righteous Banner was raised, Gaozu appointed him on commission as Acting Army Aide on the Suppressing Army staff. Soon he joined the staff of the Grand Marshal, Prince of Langya; then on account of public business he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Righteous Banner uprising began, Gaozu commissioned him as acting aide on the Suppressing Army staff. He soon joined the staff of the Prince of Langya as Grand Marshal, but was later dismissed on official grounds.

sentences.zh: 頃之，復補主簿。

translations.literal: Before long he was again appointed Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was reappointed chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 豫討桓玄功，封南郡州陵縣五等侯。

translations.literal: For participating in the campaign against Huan Xuan he was enfeoffed as Fifth-Rank Marquis of Zhouling county in Nan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: For his service in the campaign against Huan Xuan he was enfeoffed as fifth-rank Marquis of Zhouling in Nan commandery.

sentences.zh: 孟昶建威府司馬，中書侍郎，中軍太尉從事中郎，征西大將軍道規長史、南郡太守，尋轉太尉諮議參軍，領錄事，遷長史，入為侍中，大司馬，從府公北伐，拜洛陽園陵，進至潼關。

translations.literal: He served as Staff Officer of the Establishing Might Commandery under Meng Chang; Palace Secretary Attendant; Attendant on the Central Army Grand Commander; Chief of Staff and Administrator of Nan commandery under the Western Expedition Grand General Daogui; soon transferred to Advisory Staff Member under the Grand Commander, leading recorder duties; promoted to Chief of Staff; entered court as Palace Attendant on the Grand Marshal staff; followed the Prince on the northern expedition; paid respects at the Luoyang imperial tombs; advanced as far as Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: He served as staff officer of the Establishing Might Commandery under Meng Chang, then as Palace Secretary Attendant, then as an attendant on the Grand Commander's Central Army staff, then as chief of staff and Administrator of Nan commandery under the Western Expedition Grand General Daogui. He was soon transferred to the Grand Commander's advisory staff with responsibility for record-keeping, then promoted to chief of staff. He entered court service as palace attendant on the Grand Marshal's staff, accompanied the prince on the northern expedition, performed obeisance at the Luoyang imperial tombs, and advanced as far as Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 還領寧遠將軍、琅邪內史、本州大中正。

translations.literal: On returning he held concurrently the post of General of Ningyuan, Administrator of Langya, and Senior Arbiter of his native province.
translations.idiomatic: On returning he was made concurrently General Who Pacifies the Distance, Administrator of Langya, and Senior Arbiter of his native province.

sentences.zh: 高祖命大司馬府、琅邪國事，一以委焉。

translations.literal: Gaozu charged him with all matters of the Grand Marshal's commandery seat and the State of Langya, entrusting everything to him.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu entrusted to him every affair of the Grand Marshal's headquarters and the State of Langya.

sentences.zh: 宋臺初建，為五兵尚書。

translations.literal: When the Song Platform was first established, he served as Minister of the Five Armies.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song Platform was first established, he was appointed Minister of the Five Armies.

sentences.zh: 高祖受命，轉掌度支。

translations.literal: When Gaozu received the Mandate, he was transferred to oversee the Revenue Section.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, he was put in charge of the Revenue Section.

sentences.zh: 出為義興太守，加秩中二千石，以疾去職。

translations.literal: He went out as Administrator of Yixing, with added rank at two thousand piculs in the middle grade, and left office on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Administrator of Yixing with emolument at two thousand piculs in the middle grade, but resigned because of illness.

sentences.zh: 尋拜吏部尚書，為吳郡太守。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Minister of the Masters of Writing in charge of Personnel, and served as Administrator of Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Minister of Personnel and Administrator of Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 營陽王于吳縣見害，夷臨哭盡禮。

translations.literal: When Prince of Yingyang was murdered at Wu county, Yi came to mourn and performed the full rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Yingyang was murdered at Wu county, Yi came to the funeral and observed every mourning rite.

sentences.zh: 又以兄疾去官。

translations.literal: He again left office because of his elder brother's illness.
translations.idiomatic: He again resigned when his elder brother fell ill.

sentences.zh: 復為丹陽尹，吏部尚書，加散騎常侍，遷右僕射。

translations.literal: He again became Intendant of Danyang, Minister of Personnel, was given the additional post of Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, and was transferred to Right Vice Minister.
translations.idiomatic: He served again as intendant of Danyang and Minister of Personnel, was made regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, and was promoted to right vice minister.

sentences.zh: 夷美風儀，善舉止，歷任以和簡著稱。

translations.literal: Yi had fine bearing and deportment, was skilled in conduct, and in every post was known for harmony and simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: Yi had a graceful presence and excellent manners, and in every office he was praised for his mild, unassuming style.

sentences.zh: 出為湘州刺史，加散騎常侍，未之職，病卒，時年四十八。

translations.literal: He went out as Inspector of Xiangzhou with the additional post of Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry; before taking up the post he died of illness, aged forty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as Inspector of Xiangzhou with the additional rank of regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, but died of illness before taking office, at the age of forty-eight.

sentences.zh: 遺命薄斂蔬奠，務存儉約。

translations.literal: His testament ordered a meager encoffinment with vegetable offerings, striving to preserve frugality.
translations.idiomatic: In his final instructions he called for a plain burial with simple vegetable offerings, insisting on austerity.

sentences.zh: 追贈前將軍，本官如故。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given Forward General; his former offices were unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Forward General, with his former titles confirmed.

sentences.zh: 子湛，別有傳。

translations.literal: His son Zhan has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhan is treated in a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：為國之道，食不如信，立人之要，先質後文。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: In the way of governing a state, food is not equal to trust; in establishing men, substance comes before ornament.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: In governing a state, sustenance is less important than trust; in raising up men, character must come before polish.

sentences.zh: 士君子當以體正為基，蹈義為本，然後飾以藝能，文以禮樂，苟或難備，不若文不足而質有餘也。

translations.literal: The gentleman should take upright substance as foundation and treading righteousness as root, then adorn with talent and ornament with ritual and music; if both cannot be fully attained, it is better to lack ornament and have substance in surplus.
translations.idiomatic: A gentleman should ground himself in moral integrity and root himself in righteousness, then adorn that foundation with talent and grace it with ritual and music; if he cannot have both, it is better to lack polish than to lack substance.

sentences.zh: 是以小心翼翼，可祗事於上帝，嗇夫喋喋，終不離於虎圈。

translations.literal: Therefore the cautious and reverent may serve Heaven; the petty and clamorous will never leave the tiger's den.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the reverent and careful may serve Heaven, while the petty and quarrelsome never escape the tiger's cage.

sentences.zh: 江夷、謝方明、謝弘微、王惠、王球，學義之美，未足以成名，而貞心雅體，廷臣所罕及。

translations.literal: Jiang Yi, Xie Fangming, Xie Hongwei, Wang Hui, and Wang Qiu—the beauty of their learning and righteousness was not enough to make them famous, yet their steadfast hearts and refined bearing were rarely matched among court ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Yi, Xie Fangming, Xie Hongwei, Wang Hui, and Wang Qiu were learned and upright, yet not famous for brilliance; their constancy and refined character, however, few courtiers could equal.

sentences.zh: 《詩》云：「溫溫恭人，惟德之基，」信矣！

translations.literal: The Odes say: "Gentle and reverent is the man—virtue's foundation,"—how true!
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Odes says, "Gentle and reverent is the man—he is virtue's foundation"—and how true that is!
